attributes.description: Reference to a switching order in the DMS (Distribution Management System) or EMS that is coordinated with this dispatch instruction. Used when dispatch is part of a planned switching sequence.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-001; NERC TOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-004; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: generating_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the generating unit or controllable resource to which this dispatch instruction is directed. Links to the asset registry in Maximo or GIS.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 860; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to an associated outage or reliability event in the OMS (Outage Management System) that triggered or is related to this dispatch instruction. Populated for reliability-driven dispatches.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-001; NERC TOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: operator_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-004; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.description: The SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) telemetry point identifier associated with the generating unit's MW output measurement in OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to correlate dispatch instructions with real-time telemetry data.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007; OSIsoft PI Historian; NIST SP 800-82

attributes.name: acknowledgment_status
attributes.description: Status of the generating unit or resource operator's acknowledgment of this dispatch instruction. Pending indicates awaiting response; acknowledged confirms receipt; not_acknowledged indicates no response within the required window; rejected indicates the resource declined the instruction.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-001; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: acknowledgment_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the generating unit operator or automated system acknowledged receipt of this dispatch instruction.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-001; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: agc_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential number assigned by the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system for this dispatch instruction within a given AGC scan cycle. Used to correlate instructions to AGC telemetry cycles in OSIsoft PI Historian.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; IEEE Std 1547

attributes.name: co2_emission_rate_lb_per_mwh
attributes.description: The estimated CO2 emission rate for the dispatched generating unit at the instructed MW setpoint, expressed in pounds per MWh. Used for environmental compliance reporting to EPA and state regulators.
attributes.references: EPA eGRID; EPA Clean Air Act; DOE EIA; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the generating unit complied with this dispatch instruction within the required response time and MW tolerance. True if compliant; False if non-compliant. Used for NERC BAL reliability reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: contingency_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the N-1 or N-2 contingency scenario that triggered this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Used for post-contingency analysis and NERC reliability event reporting.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was first captured in the Silver Layer data product. Audit trail field for data lineage and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82; FASB ASC 980

attributes.name: demand_response_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Demand Response (DR) resource rather than a traditional generating unit. True when the controllable resource is a DR program participant.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; NERC BAL-001; DOE DR guidelines

attributes.name: der_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Distributed Energy Resource (DER) such as rooftop solar, battery storage, or small-scale generation managed via DERMS.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222; IEEE Std 1547; NERC BAL-001; DOE DERMS guidelines

attributes.name: dispatch_reason
attributes.description: The primary reason for issuing this dispatch instruction. Economic dispatch optimizes cost; reliability dispatch addresses grid stability; regulation dispatch supports frequency control; emergency dispatch responds to contingency events; voltage_support addresses reactive power needs; reserve dispatch activates operating reserves. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: economic|reliability|regulation|emergency|voltage_support|reserve — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888; LMP market rules

attributes.name: dispatch_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the dispatch instruction was generated automatically by the AGC system or issued manually by an EMS operator. Automatic instructions originate from AGC scan cycles; manual instructions are operator-initiated.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: effective_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the dispatch instruction is expected to take effect at the generating unit. May differ from instruction_timestamp due to ramp lead time or scheduling offset.

attributes.name: energy_source_type
attributes.description: The primary energy source type of the dispatched generating unit or resource. Used for generation mix reporting, renewable energy tracking, and REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) accounting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fossil_fuel|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|battery_storage|demand_response|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EIA Form 860; EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction expires or is superseded if not acknowledged or executed. After this time, the instruction is considered void.

attributes.name: frequency_regulation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction is associated with frequency regulation service (AGC regulation signal). True when the instruction is part of a regulation up/down signal from the balancing authority.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755

attributes.name: fuel_type
attributes.description: The specific fuel type consumed by the dispatched generating unit. Used for fuel cost allocation, emissions reporting, and EPA compliance. 'none' for non-fuel resources such as wind, solar, or demand response. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|oil|uranium|water|wind|solar|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; EPA Clean Air Act; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: heat_rate_btu_per_kwh
attributes.description: The heat rate of the generating unit at the dispatched MW setpoint, expressed in British Thermal Units per kilowatt-hour (BTU/kWh). Used for fuel consumption estimation, emissions calculations, and economic dispatch optimization.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; FERC Order 888; EPA Clean Air Act

attributes.name: instruction_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the dispatch instruction, used in operator logs, audit trails, and regulatory filings. Format: EMS-DISP-YYYY-NNNNNN.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; NERC EOP-001

attributes.name: instruction_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the dispatch instruction. Tracks the workflow from issuance through acknowledgment, execution, and completion or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: issued|acknowledged|executing|completed|cancelled|rejected — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC EOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: instruction_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the EMS issued this dispatch instruction to the generating unit or controllable resource. This is the principal business event timestamp.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; NERC EOP-001

attributes.name: lmp_at_dispatch
attributes.description: The Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in dollars per MWh at the dispatch node at the time this instruction was issued. Used for economic dispatch evaluation and post-dispatch settlement.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO LMP methodology

attributes.name: lmp_node_code
attributes.description: Reference to the pricing node at which the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) applies for this dispatch instruction. Used for economic dispatch optimization and settlement calculations.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO LMP methodology

attributes.name: market_interval_code
attributes.description: Reference to the energy market interval (Day-Ahead Market or Real-Time Market) associated with this dispatch instruction. Links to the market scheduling system or ETRM (Allegro) interval record.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO tariff; LMP market rules

attributes.name: market_type
attributes.description: The energy market context under which this dispatch instruction is issued. DAM (Day-Ahead Market), RTM (Real-Time Market), bilateral contract, self-schedule, or none for purely reliability-driven dispatches.
attributes.references: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO tariff; LMP market rules

attributes.name: mvar_setpoint
attributes.description: The target reactive power output level in Megavars (MVAR) instructed for voltage support purposes. Applicable when dispatch_reason is voltage_support or when reactive dispatch is co-optimized.
attributes.references: NERC VAR-001; NERC VAR-002; FERC Order 888

attributes.name: mw_actual_response
attributes.description: The actual MW output achieved by the generating unit in response to this dispatch instruction, as measured by SCADA telemetry from OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to assess dispatch compliance and unit performance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; OSIsoft PI Historian; EIA Form 923

attributes.name: mw_compliance_deviation
attributes.description: The difference in MW between the instructed setpoint and the actual response (mw_actual_response minus mw_setpoint). Positive values indicate over-generation; negative values indicate under-generation. Used for NERC compliance analysis.

attributes.name: mw_delta
attributes.description: The change in MW output instructed by this dispatch (mw_setpoint minus mw_setpoint_prior). Positive values indicate an increase in generation; negative values indicate a decrease. Used for ramp compliance analysis.

attributes.name: mw_setpoint
attributes.description: The target real power output level in Megawatts (MW) that the generating unit or controllable resource is instructed to achieve. This is the principal quantitative dispatch directive.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1547; EIA Form 923

attributes.name: mw_setpoint_prior
attributes.description: The MW setpoint that was in effect immediately before this dispatch instruction was issued. Used to calculate the MW delta and assess ramp requirements.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the EMS operator at the time of dispatch. May include context for manual overrides, reliability concerns, or coordination with other control areas.

attributes.name: pi_tag_name
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name for the real-time MW output data stream of the dispatched generating unit. Enables direct linkage between dispatch instructions and PI Historian time-series data for operational analytics.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82

attributes.name: ramp_rate_mw_per_min
attributes.description: The instructed rate of change in MW output, expressed in Megawatts per minute (MW/min), at which the generating unit should ramp to the new setpoint. Derived from unit capability and AGC parameters.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1547

attributes.name: regulation_direction
attributes.description: Direction of frequency regulation service associated with this dispatch instruction. 'up' indicates regulation up (increase output); 'down' indicates regulation down (decrease output); 'none' for non-regulation dispatches.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Free-text or coded reason provided by the resource operator when a dispatch instruction is rejected or not acknowledged. Used for reliability event analysis and operator performance review.

attributes.name: reserve_type
attributes.description: Type of operating reserve being activated by this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Spinning reserves are online and synchronized; non-spinning reserves can be brought online within 10 minutes; supplemental reserves provide longer-term backup.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO tariff

attributes.name: response_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the generating unit reached or was confirmed to be at the instructed MW setpoint, as recorded by SCADA telemetry.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The originating operational system that generated this dispatch instruction. EMS for Energy Management System automated dispatch; AGC for Automatic Generation Control; DMS for Distribution Management System; OMS for Outage Management System; DERMS for Distributed Energy Resource Management System; manual for operator-entered instructions.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC CIP-007

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was last modified in the Silver Layer data product. Used for incremental data processing and audit trail.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82; FASB ASC 980

products.name: load_forecast
products.description: Stores short-term (hourly/daily), medium-term (weekly/monthly), and persistence forecasts produced by the EMS forecasting engine for the balancing area and control zones. Includes forecasted MW demand by interval, weather-adjusted baseline, peak demand estimate, confidence interval, forecast model version, and actual vs. forecast variance for accuracy tracking. Used for unit commitment, interchange scheduling, DR dispatch planning, and next-day operations planning.

attributes.name: load_forecast_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each load forecast record in the balancing area Energy Management System (EMS) forecasting engine. Primary key for the load_forecast data product.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the NERC-defined Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this load forecast was produced. The balancing area is the fundamental geographic and operational unit for which the EMS maintains load-generation balance. Links to the balancing area master reference product.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: control_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific control zone or load zone within the balancing area for which this forecast applies. Control zones represent sub-areas of the transmission system with distinct load characteristics, used for Locational Marginal Price (LMP) and zonal load forecasting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

attributes.name: weather_forecast_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.weather_forecast. Business justification: Load forecasts are derived from a specific weather forecast; FK links forecast source.

attributes.name: actual_demand_mw
attributes.description: The observed actual electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the forecast interval, populated post-interval from SCADA telemetry or OSIsoft PI Historian. Null until the interval has elapsed and actuals are available. Used for forecast accuracy tracking and model performance evaluation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: confidence_interval_lower_mw
attributes.description: The lower bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the minimum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for probabilistic unit commitment and reserve margin planning.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

attributes.name: confidence_interval_upper_mw
attributes.description: The upper bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the maximum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for contingency planning and operating reserve determination.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

attributes.name: confidence_level_pct
attributes.description: The statistical confidence level expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90.00, 95.00) associated with the confidence interval bounds. Indicates the probability that actual demand will fall within the stated confidence interval bounds.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

attributes.name: cooling_degree_days
attributes.description: The number of Cooling Degree Days (CDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature exceeds 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify cooling-driven electrical demand.
attributes.references: EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards; IRP regulatory filings

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording when this load forecast record was first persisted into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and SLA compliance tracking. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: NERC CIP-008; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FASB ASC 980

attributes.name: day_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecast day by its load profile category. Weekday, weekend, and holiday designations drive distinct load shape patterns in the EMS forecasting model. Peak day and off-peak day classifications support Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate analysis.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; TOU/CPP rate tariff definitions

attributes.name: der_generation_forecast_mw
attributes.description: The forecasted generation output in Megawatts (MW) from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage, and small-scale generation within the distribution system. Subtracted from gross load to derive net load. Sourced from DERMS forecasting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222; NERC BAL-001; DERMS operational standards

attributes.name: dr_dispatched_mw
attributes.description: The amount of Demand Response (DR) capacity in Megawatts (MW) that has been dispatched or is planned to be dispatched during this forecast interval. Represents load reduction committed through DR programs, reducing the net load the grid must serve. Used for DR dispatch planning and DERMS coordination.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745; NERC BAL-001; DERMS operational standards

attributes.name: forecast_date
attributes.description: The calendar date for which the load forecast applies. For day-ahead forecasts this is the operating day being forecasted. Used for daily operations planning, Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling, and next-day unit commitment.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_error_mw
attributes.description: The absolute difference between forecasted demand and actual demand in Megawatts (MW), calculated as actual_demand_mw minus forecasted_demand_mw. Positive values indicate under-forecasting; negative values indicate over-forecasting. Populated post-interval for accuracy tracking.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_error_pct
attributes.description: The forecast error expressed as a percentage of actual demand, calculated as (actual_demand_mw - forecasted_demand_mw) / actual_demand_mw * 100. Used as the primary KPI for EMS forecasting model accuracy assessment and NERC compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_type
attributes.description: Classification of the forecast by its planning horizon. Short-term covers hourly/daily intervals; medium-term covers weekly/monthly; persistence uses the last observed value as the forecast; day-ahead supports Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling; real-time supports Real-Time Market (RTM) dispatch. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: short_term|medium_term|long_term|persistence|day_ahead|real_time — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_humidity_pct
attributes.description: The forecasted relative humidity percentage used as a secondary weather input to the load forecasting model. Humidity affects the heat index and cooling load, particularly for residential and commercial air conditioning demand.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

attributes.name: forecast_interval_end
attributes.description: The ending date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. Together with forecast_interval_start, defines the precise time window of the forecast. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_interval_start
attributes.description: The beginning date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. For hourly forecasts this marks the top of the hour; for daily forecasts this marks midnight. Used for unit commitment scheduling, interchange scheduling, and DR dispatch planning. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_model_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the load forecasting algorithm or model used to produce this forecast (e.g., regression-based, neural network, ensemble). Supports model governance, audit trail, and comparison of forecast accuracy across different modeling approaches in the EMS.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: forecast_model_version
attributes.description: The version string of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast (e.g., '3.2.1'). Enables traceability of forecast outputs to specific model releases, supporting model validation, regulatory audit, and accuracy benchmarking.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: forecast_model_version_code
attributes.description: Reference to the specific version of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast. Enables accuracy tracking across model versions, supports model governance, and facilitates comparison of forecast performance between model iterations.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: forecast_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, qualitative adjustments, or override justifications applied to this forecast record by EMS operators. Captures manual interventions, special event adjustments (e.g., major sporting events, industrial shutdowns), or model override rationale for audit and review purposes.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; internal EMS operational procedures

attributes.name: forecast_run_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier assigned by the EMS forecasting engine to uniquely identify a specific forecast run or batch. Used to group all interval records produced in a single forecast execution cycle. Aligns with OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS run identifiers.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: forecast_run_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the EMS forecasting engine initiated and completed the forecast run that produced this record. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the forecast was generated, distinct from the interval being forecasted. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: forecast_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Draft indicates the forecast is being generated; published indicates it has been released for operational use; superseded indicates a newer forecast run has replaced it; archived indicates it has been retained for historical accuracy tracking; cancelled indicates the run was aborted.

attributes.name: forecast_temperature_f
attributes.description: The forecasted ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit used as the primary weather input to the load forecasting model for this interval. Temperature is the dominant weather driver of electrical load in most utility service territories.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

attributes.name: forecasted_demand_mw
attributes.description: The primary forecasted electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the specified interval. This is the principal quantitative output of the EMS forecasting engine, used for unit commitment, interchange scheduling, and next-day operations planning.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; NERC MOD-031

attributes.name: heating_degree_days
attributes.description: The number of Heating Degree Days (HDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature falls below 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify heating-driven electrical and gas demand.
attributes.references: EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards; IRP regulatory filings

attributes.name: interchange_schedule_mw
attributes.description: The scheduled net interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas or the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO)/Independent System Operator (ISO) for this forecast interval. Positive values indicate net imports; negative values indicate net exports. Used in balancing area control and unit commitment.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC INT-006

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The length of the forecast interval in minutes (e.g., 15, 30, 60, 1440 for daily). Determines the granularity of the forecast and aligns with Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) interval data and SCADA telemetry resolution.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; AMI standards

attributes.name: is_peak_period
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval falls within a designated peak demand period as defined by the utility's tariff or operational planning criteria. Used to identify intervals requiring heightened operational attention, DR dispatch readiness, and capacity reserve verification.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; PUC tariff definitions; TOU/CPP rate structures

attributes.name: is_reliability_event
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval is associated with a declared reliability event (e.g., emergency operating condition, NERC alert, extreme weather advisory). When true, the forecast may have been produced under emergency protocols with modified model parameters.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-011; NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: manual_override_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether an EMS operator manually overrode the model-generated forecast value for this interval. When true, the forecasted_demand_mw reflects an operator-adjusted value rather than the raw model output. Supports audit trail and model accuracy analysis.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; internal EMS operational procedures

attributes.name: net_load_forecast_mw
attributes.description: The forecasted net load in Megawatts (MW) after subtracting Distributed Energy Resources (DER) generation (e.g., rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage) from gross forecasted demand. Net load is the actual generation requirement that dispatchable resources must meet. Critical for unit commitment and interchange scheduling.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; DERMS operational standards; EIA Form 930

attributes.name: operating_day
attributes.description: The NERC-defined operating day (midnight to midnight local time) to which this forecast record belongs. Distinct from forecast_date in that it represents the grid operations scheduling day used by the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) for market and reliability purposes.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

attributes.name: operating_reserve_requirement_mw
attributes.description: The minimum operating reserve requirement in Megawatts (MW) for this forecast interval, derived from the forecasted load and NERC reliability standards. Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves required to maintain grid reliability. Used for unit commitment and capacity planning.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: peak_demand_estimate_mw
attributes.description: The estimated peak electrical demand in Megawatts (MW) expected within the forecast period. Critical for capacity planning, reserve margin calculations, and Demand Response (DR) dispatch planning. Used in General Rate Case (GRC) filings and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submissions.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; PUC rate case filings

attributes.name: regulatory_reporting_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast record is designated for inclusion in regulatory reporting submissions (e.g., EIA Form 930, FERC filings, NERC reliability assessments, PUC rate case filings). Supports automated extraction of reportable forecast data for compliance workflows.
attributes.references: EIA Form 930; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; PUC reporting requirements

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: The code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market in which this balancing area participates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP). Determines the market rules, scheduling protocols, and reporting requirements applicable to this forecast.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

attributes.name: season
attributes.description: The utility-defined operating season for the forecast interval. Seasonal classification drives load shape selection in the EMS forecasting model and aligns with seasonal rate structures, capacity planning periods, and NERC reliability assessments.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; PUC seasonal rate filings

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the operational system of record that produced or supplied this load forecast record. Supports data lineage and provenance tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Values correspond to the utility's operational systems including the Energy Management System (EMS), SCADA, OSIsoft PI Historian, Distribution Management System (DMS), Outage Management System (OMS), and DERMS. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EMS|SCADA|PI_HISTORIAN|DMS|OMS|DERMS|MANUAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NIST Smart Grid Framework; NERC CIP-008; FERC Order 764

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this load forecast record, such as when actual demand values were populated post-interval or when the forecast status was updated. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
attributes.references: NERC CIP-008; NIST Smart Grid Framework

attributes.name: weather_adjusted_baseline_mw
attributes.description: The weather-normalized baseline load demand in Megawatts (MW), representing what demand would be under normal or reference weather conditions. Used to isolate weather-driven load variability from underlying demand trends for regulatory reporting and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) analysis.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; IRP regulatory filings

attributes.name: weather_station_code
attributes.description: Reference to the primary weather station or weather data source used to supply temperature, humidity, and other meteorological inputs to the load forecasting model for this forecast interval. Weather normalization is a core component of EMS load forecasting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

products.name: frequency_regulation_event
products.description: Captures frequency regulation events, ACE (Area Control Error) exceedances, AGC response actions, and serves as the single source of truth for all energy balance and frequency compliance data for the balancing area. Records include: frequency deviations from 60 Hz, CPS1/CPS2/BAAL compliance metrics, regulation reserve deployment, and corrective actions taken. Also stores hourly and sub-hourly energy accounting: total generation (MWh), total load (MWh), net interchange (MWh), system losses, and ACE values by interval. Supports NERC BAL-001 (real power balancing), BAL-002 (disturbance control), BAL-003 (frequency response), energy balance reporting for RTO/ISO settlement, and operational energy accounting. This is the authoritative product for all ACE-related data, frequency compliance, and energy balance records.

attributes.name: frequency_regulation_event_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each frequency regulation event record in the balancing area. Primary key for this data product.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area (BAA) in which this frequency regulation event occurred. Links to the balancing area master record for geographic and operational context.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: crew_member_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operations control room operator who acknowledged, responded to, or closed this frequency regulation event. Provides accountability traceability for manual operator interventions and NERC compliance documentation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC CIP-006

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operations control room operator who acknowledged, responded to, or closed this frequency regulation event. Provides accountability traceability for manual operator interventions and NERC compliance documentation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC CIP-006

attributes.name: regulatory_rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Frequency regulation performance is reported in rate‑case filings; linking each event to the rate case enables required reporting.

attributes.name: ace_threshold_mw
attributes.description: The ACE threshold in Megawatts (MW) that, when exceeded, triggers a compliance event or corrective action. Derived from the Balancing Authority's frequency bias setting and NERC BAL-001 control performance standards.

attributes.name: ace_value_mw
attributes.description: Instantaneous Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the event. ACE represents the difference between actual and scheduled net interchange, adjusted for frequency bias. This is the authoritative ACE measurement for NERC BAL-001 real power balancing compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-005; EMS/SCADA; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: actual_interchange_mw
attributes.description: The actual measured net interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas at the time of the event, as recorded by SCADA/EMS metering. The difference between actual and scheduled interchange is a primary component of the ACE calculation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-005; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: agc_response_mw
attributes.description: Total Megawatts (MW) of generation adjustment dispatched by the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system in response to this frequency regulation event. Represents the corrective generation signal sent to participating generating units.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-003; GE PowerOn EMS

attributes.name: baal_exceedance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) Exceedance Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) was exceeded during this event. True if ACE exceeded the BAAL threshold as defined in NERC BAL-001-2, triggering mandatory corrective action and potential compliance reporting.

attributes.name: baal_high_mw
attributes.description: The upper Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary.

attributes.name: baal_low_mw
attributes.description: The lower Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary on the under-generation side.

attributes.name: control_area_code
attributes.description: NERC-assigned alphanumeric code identifying the Balancing Authority control area where the event occurred. Used in NERC compliance filings, RTO/ISO interchange scheduling, and energy balance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC; NERC Reliability Standards

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Narrative description of the corrective actions taken by the EMS/AGC system or grid operators to restore frequency and ACE to within compliance limits. Includes AGC dispatch instructions, manual operator interventions, and emergency procedures. Required for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control documentation.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn EMS

attributes.name: cps1_score
attributes.description: NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE divided by the frequency error, with a minimum compliance threshold of 100%. Values below 100% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.

attributes.name: cps2_score
attributes.description: NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS2 measures the 10-minute average ACE against the L10 limit, with a minimum compliance threshold of 90%. Values below 90% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time (UTC) when this frequency regulation event record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and ETL reconciliation.
attributes.references: NIST Smart Grid Framework; Internal Data Governance Policy

attributes.name: disturbance_cause
attributes.description: Root cause classification of the frequency regulation event or disturbance. Used for post-event analysis, NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard reporting, and operational reliability improvement. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation_trip|load_loss|transmission_fault|interchange_error|equipment_failure|weather_event|unknown — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC Event Analysis; FERC

attributes.name: duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total elapsed duration of the frequency regulation event in seconds, calculated from event_start_timestamp to event_end_timestamp. Used for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard compliance assessment and operational performance reporting.

attributes.name: ems_event_code
attributes.description: The native event identifier assigned by the Energy Management System (EMS) — specifically GE PowerOn — for this frequency regulation event. Used for cross-referencing between the lakehouse Silver layer and the operational EMS source system for audit and reconciliation purposes.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced EMS; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: event_code
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned to this frequency regulation event, used in NERC compliance filings, RTO/ISO settlement reports, and operational logs. Format: FRE-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (UTC) when the frequency regulation event concluded and normal operating conditions were restored. Null if the event is still active. Used to compute event duration for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control standard compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: event_severity
attributes.description: Operational severity classification of the frequency regulation event based on the magnitude of frequency deviation, ACE exceedance, and system impact. Used for prioritizing operator response, escalation workflows, and post-event reliability analysis.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; NERC Event Analysis; GE PowerOn OMS/DMS

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (UTC) when the frequency regulation event began, as recorded by the Energy Management System (EMS) or SCADA historian. This is the principal real-world event time used for NERC compliance interval calculations and RTO/ISO settlement.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-003; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the frequency regulation event record. 'active' indicates the event is ongoing; 'resolved' indicates corrective action has restored normal frequency; 'under_review' indicates post-event analysis is in progress; 'reported' indicates the event has been submitted to NERC/RTO; 'closed' indicates all follow-up actions are complete.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the frequency regulation event. Distinguishes between frequency deviations from 60 Hz, Area Control Error (ACE) exceedances, Automatic Generation Control (AGC) response actions, disturbance control events, regulation reserve deployments, and Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) exceedances. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: frequency_deviation|ace_exceedance|agc_response|disturbance_control|regulation_reserve_deployment|baal_exceedance — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; NERC BAL-005

attributes.name: frequency_bias_setting_mw_per_hz
attributes.description: The balancing authority's frequency bias setting in Megawatts per Hertz (MW/Hz) in effect during this event. Used in the ACE calculation formula: ACE = (NIA - NIS) - 10B(FA - FS). Must be reported to NERC and the RTO/ISO per BAL-001 and BAL-005 requirements.

attributes.name: frequency_deviation_hz
attributes.description: Magnitude of frequency deviation from the 60 Hz nominal in Hertz (Hz). Positive values indicate over-frequency; negative values indicate under-frequency. Key metric for NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligation compliance and disturbance analysis.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003; NERC PRC-024; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: frequency_nadir_hz
attributes.description: The lowest instantaneous system frequency in Hertz (Hz) recorded during this event, representing the frequency nadir following a generation loss or load increase disturbance. Critical metric for NERC BAL-003 frequency response adequacy assessment.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003; NERC PRC-024; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: frequency_response_mw_per_hz
attributes.description: The balancing authority's measured frequency response in Megawatts per Hertz (MW/Hz) during this event. Compared against the NERC-assigned Frequency Response Obligation (FRO) to assess BAL-003 compliance. A more negative value indicates stronger frequency response.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003; NERC Frequency Response Initiative

attributes.name: interconnection_name
attributes.description: Name of the North American electrical interconnection (synchronous grid) within which this frequency regulation event occurred. Determines the nominal frequency standard (60 Hz) and the pool of balancing authorities sharing frequency response obligations.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003; NERC Reliability Standards; DOE

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: End timestamp (UTC) of the energy accounting interval associated with this record. Paired with interval_start_timestamp to define the precise measurement window for energy balance and ACE compliance calculations.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Start timestamp (UTC) of the energy accounting interval associated with this record. Used to align hourly and sub-hourly energy balance data (generation, load, interchange, losses) with RTO/ISO settlement periods and NERC BAL-001 compliance measurement windows.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: nerc_reportable_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this frequency regulation event meets the threshold for mandatory reporting to NERC under applicable reliability standards (BAL-001, BAL-002, BAL-003). True if the event must be included in NERC compliance filings or event analysis submissions.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; NERC Rules of Procedure

attributes.name: nerc_violation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event resulted in a confirmed violation of a NERC reliability standard (e.g., BAL-001 CPS1/CPS2 non-compliance, BAL-002 disturbance control failure, BAL-003 frequency response obligation shortfall). True triggers mandatory NERC self-report or enforcement action.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; NERC Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (CMEP)

attributes.name: net_interchange_mwh
attributes.description: Net energy interchange with neighboring balancing areas during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Positive values indicate net export; negative values indicate net import. Core component of the ACE calculation and energy balance accounting per NERC BAL-001.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-005; EIA Form 930; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: pi_tag_reference
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name or tag path associated with the primary frequency or ACE measurement for this event. Enables direct traceability from the Silver layer record back to the real-time operational data stream in the PI Historian for validation and reprocessing.

attributes.name: regulation_down_mw
attributes.description: Megawatts (MW) of regulation-down reserve deployed during this event to decrease generation output and correct an over-frequency or positive ACE condition. Reported separately for RTO/ISO market settlement and NERC BAL-002 compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: regulation_reserve_deployed_mw
attributes.description: Total regulation reserve capacity deployed in Megawatts (MW) during this event. Includes both regulation-up and regulation-down resources activated to restore ACE to within compliance limits. Used for RTO/ISO settlement and reserve adequacy reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: regulation_up_mw
attributes.description: Megawatts (MW) of regulation-up reserve deployed during this event to increase generation output and correct an under-frequency or negative ACE condition. Reported separately for RTO/ISO market settlement and NERC BAL-002 compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: reporting_interval_type
attributes.description: The sub-hourly or hourly interval granularity for energy accounting data associated with this event record. Determines the resolution of generation, load, interchange, and ACE values stored. Aligns with RTO/ISO settlement interval requirements and NERC BAL-001 compliance measurement periods.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 890; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) ID
attributes.description: Reference to the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) under whose market rules and settlement protocols this frequency regulation event is reported. Links to the RTO/ISO master record for market context.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000; NERC BAL-001; RTO/ISO Tariffs

attributes.name: scheduled_interchange_mw
attributes.description: The net scheduled interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas at the time of the event, as agreed through the interchange scheduling process. Used in the ACE calculation and compared against actual interchange to determine the interchange component of ACE.

attributes.name: settlement_interval_code
attributes.description: Reference to the RTO/ISO market settlement interval record associated with this energy balance event. Links frequency regulation and energy accounting data to the corresponding Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or Real-Time Market (RTM) settlement period.
attributes.references: FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols; Allegro ETRM

attributes.name: system_frequency_hz
attributes.description: Measured system frequency in Hertz (Hz) at the time of the event trigger. Nominal value is 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections. Deviations from 60 Hz trigger frequency regulation responses per NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligations.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003; NERC PRC-024; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: system_losses_mwh
attributes.description: Estimated transmission and distribution system losses in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) during the event interval. Used in energy balance reconciliation: Generation = Load + Net Interchange + Losses. Supports NERC BAL-001 energy accounting and EIA reporting.

attributes.name: total_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy generated within the balancing area during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Authoritative value for energy balance accounting, RTO/ISO settlement, and NERC BAL-001 real power balancing compliance.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: total_load_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy consumed by load within the balancing area during the event interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Used for energy balance verification, RTO/ISO settlement, and NERC BAL-001 compliance reporting.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; RTO/ISO Settlement Protocols; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time (UTC) when this frequency regulation event record was most recently modified in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Tracks post-event corrections, operator annotations, and compliance status updates.
attributes.references: NIST Smart Grid Framework; Internal Data Governance Policy

products.name: voltage_control_action
products.description: Records operator and automated voltage control actions taken within the grid including capacitor bank switching, reactor switching, tap changer adjustments, and reactive power dispatch. Captures target bus, pre-action voltage (kV), post-action voltage (kV), action type, initiating condition, and operator or automation source. Supports voltage profile compliance and post-event review.

attributes.name: voltage_control_action_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the voltage control action record.

attributes.name: approver_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.

attributes.name: approver_id
attributes.description: Reference to the supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Voltage control actions occur within a balancing area; FK replaces textual code.

attributes.name: bus_id
attributes.description: Reference to the electrical bus that was the target of the voltage control action.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operator who initiated the manual voltage control action. Null if action was automated.

attributes.name: ems_dispatch_ems_dispatch_instruction_id
attributes.description: The dispatch instruction identifier from the Energy Management System that authorized or triggered this voltage control action.

attributes.name: ems_dispatch_instruction_id
attributes.description: The dispatch instruction identifier from the Energy Management System that authorized or triggered this voltage control action.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to an outage record if this voltage control action was related to outage management or restoration activities.

attributes.name: outage_gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to an outage record if this voltage control action was related to outage management or restoration activities.

attributes.name: primary_voltage_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operator who initiated the manual voltage control action. Null if action was automated.

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific control device (capacitor bank, reactor, tap changer, or reactive power source) that was operated.

attributes.name: reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to a reliability event record if this voltage control action was taken in response to a grid reliability event or contingency.

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: Reference to the SCADA monitoring point where the voltage control action was executed.

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substation where the voltage control action occurred.

attributes.name: verified_by_operator_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the operator who verified the successful completion and effectiveness of the voltage control action.

attributes.name: action_duration_seconds
attributes.description: The time in seconds from action initiation to completion or failure.

attributes.name: action_mode
attributes.description: Indicates whether the voltage control action was initiated manually by an operator, automatically by control system, scheduled as part of planned operations, or triggered by emergency conditions.

attributes.name: action_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments entered by the operator or system regarding the voltage control action, including justification, observations, or special circumstances.

attributes.name: action_priority
attributes.description: The operational priority level assigned to the voltage control action based on the severity of the voltage deviation and potential impact on grid reliability.

attributes.name: action_status
attributes.description: The execution status of the voltage control action indicating whether it completed successfully, failed, partially completed, was aborted, or is pending verification.

attributes.name: action_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the voltage control action was executed in the grid.

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: The type of voltage control action performed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: capacitor_bank_switch_on|capacitor_bank_switch_off|reactor_switch_on|reactor_switch_off|tap_changer_raise|tap_changer_lower|reactive_power_increase|reactive_power_decrease|voltage_regulator_adjust — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_c
attributes.description: The ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at the substation location at the time of the voltage control action.

attributes.name: approval_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the voltage control action required supervisory or reliability coordinator approval before execution.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when supervisory approval was granted for the voltage control action. Null if no approval was required.

attributes.name: automation_system_source
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the automated control system that initiated the voltage control action (e.g., DMS, DERMS, voltage regulator controller). Null if action was manual.

attributes.name: capacitor_bank_mvar
attributes.description: The reactive power rating in megavolt-amperes reactive of the capacitor bank that was switched. Null if action did not involve a capacitor bank.

attributes.name: control_algorithm
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the control algorithm or logic used to determine the voltage control action (e.g., volt-var optimization, conservation voltage reduction, local voltage control). Null if action was manual.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this voltage control action record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: generation_at_action_mw
attributes.description: The total real power generation in megawatts at the target bus or substation at the time the voltage control action was executed.

attributes.name: initiating_condition
attributes.description: The operational condition or event that triggered the need for voltage control action.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this voltage control action record was last updated in the system.

attributes.name: load_at_action_mw
attributes.description: The total real power load in megawatts at the target bus or substation at the time the voltage control action was executed.

attributes.name: post_action_voltage_kv
attributes.description: The voltage level in kilovolts measured at the target bus immediately after the control action was executed.

attributes.name: power_factor_post_action
attributes.description: The power factor measured at the target bus immediately after the voltage control action was executed. Value ranges from -1.0 to 1.0.

attributes.name: power_factor_pre_action
attributes.description: The power factor measured at the target bus immediately before the voltage control action was executed. Value ranges from -1.0 to 1.0.

attributes.name: pre_action_voltage_kv
attributes.description: The voltage level in kilovolts measured at the target bus immediately before the control action was executed.

attributes.name: reactive_power_change_mvar
attributes.description: The change in reactive power in megavolt-amperes reactive resulting from the voltage control action. Positive values indicate reactive power injection, negative values indicate absorption.

attributes.name: reactor_mvar
attributes.description: The reactive power rating in megavolt-amperes reactive of the reactor that was switched. Null if action did not involve a reactor.

attributes.name: switching_order_number
attributes.description: The formal switching order number associated with this voltage control action, if the action was part of a planned switching procedure.

attributes.name: tap_position_change
attributes.description: The number of tap positions changed on a tap changer device. Positive values indicate raise operations, negative values indicate lower operations. Null if action did not involve a tap changer.

attributes.name: target_voltage_kv
attributes.description: The desired voltage level in kilovolts that the control action was intended to achieve at the target bus.

attributes.name: verification_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the effectiveness of the voltage control action was verified through post-action monitoring.

attributes.name: voltage_deviation_percent
attributes.description: The percentage deviation of pre-action voltage from the nominal voltage level, calculated as ((pre_action_voltage - nominal_voltage) / nominal_voltage) * 100.

attributes.name: voltage_profile_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the post-action voltage level is within the acceptable voltage profile limits defined by regulatory standards and operational procedures.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: The prevailing weather condition at the time of the voltage control action, which may influence load patterns and voltage stability. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|snow|storm|extreme_heat|extreme_cold|fog|wind — promote to reference product]

products.name: gridops_switching_order
products.description: Manages switching orders issued by grid operations for planned and emergency switching sequences on the transmission and distribution network. Each order contains a header (order number, purpose, issuing operator, approving supervisor, execution status, safety clearances, LOTO tags) and an ordered sequence of switching steps (discrete actions on breakers, switches, and disconnects with per-step device identifier, action type, required safety tag, completion timestamp, executing operator, and sequence validation). Integrates with GE PowerOn DMS/OMS. Supports planned maintenance isolation, emergency fault restoration, and safety compliance tracking through granular step-level execution audit.

attributes.name: gridops_switching_order_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the switching order record in the grid operations system.

attributes.name: approving_supervisor_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operations supervisor or reliability coordinator who reviewed and approved this switching order for execution.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: GridOps switching orders are tied to a balancing area; FK replaces textual code.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operations control center operator who created and issued this switching order.

attributes.name: executing_crew_id
attributes.description: Reference to the field crew or operations team assigned to physically execute the switching steps in this order.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated planned outage record in the Outage Management System (OMS) if this switching order is coordinated with customer outage notifications.

attributes.name: oms_outage_gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated planned outage record in the Outage Management System (OMS) if this switching order is coordinated with customer outage notifications.

attributes.name: primary_gridops_incident_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid operations incident or reliability event that triggered this switching order, if applicable (e.g., fault, equipment failure, system disturbance).

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_order. Business justification: Regulatory cost allocation report requires linking each switching order to the purchase order that procured materials for the work.

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary substation where the switching operations will be performed.

attributes.name: warehouse_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.warehouse. Business justification: Spare parts for switching orders are drawn from specific warehouses; linking enables inventory audit and cost tracking.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated maintenance or construction work order that requires this switching order for equipment isolation or energization.

attributes.name: actual_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the final switching step in this order was completed and the order was closed.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: actual_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when execution of the first switching step in this order was initiated by the field crew or control center operator.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: affected_circuit_count
attributes.description: The number of electrical circuits (feeders, transmission lines, or distribution circuits) that will be impacted by the execution of this switching order.

attributes.name: approval_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the approving supervisor or reliability coordinator formally approved this switching order for execution.

attributes.name: approving_supervisor_name
attributes.description: Full name of the operations supervisor or reliability coordinator who approved this switching order.

attributes.name: cancellation_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why this switching order was cancelled, including operational conditions, safety concerns, or work scope changes that led to cancellation.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: cancellation_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this switching order was cancelled or voided, if applicable.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this switching order record was first created in the grid operations system.

attributes.name: emergency_restoration_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this switching order is part of an emergency restoration effort following an unplanned outage or system disturbance. True indicates emergency restoration.

attributes.name: estimated_customer_impact_count
attributes.description: The estimated number of customer accounts that may experience service interruption or voltage fluctuation during the execution of this switching order.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards - Customer Impact Assessment

attributes.name: issuing_operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the certified system operator who created and issued this switching order.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this switching order record was most recently updated or modified.

attributes.name: loto_tag_numbers
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) Tag Numbers
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) tag numbers applied to equipment as part of this switching order to ensure worker safety during de-energized work.

attributes.name: network_segment
attributes.description: The segment of the electrical network where the switching order will be executed: transmission (high-voltage bulk power), distribution (medium/low-voltage customer delivery), substation (transformation and switching facilities), or generation (power plant interconnection).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-form operational notes, special instructions, or additional context provided by the issuing operator or approving supervisor for this switching order.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: order_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique switching order number assigned by the grid operations center for tracking and reference. Format: SO-YYYYMMDD-SITE.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: order_purpose
attributes.description: Detailed business justification and operational purpose for issuing this switching order, including work scope, equipment involved, and expected outcomes.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: order_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the switching order: draft (being prepared), pending approval (awaiting supervisor review), approved (ready for execution), in progress (actively executing steps), completed (all steps executed), cancelled (order voided), or suspended (temporarily halted). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|pending_approval|approved|in_progress|completed|cancelled|suspended — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: order_type
attributes.description: Classification of the switching order based on operational purpose: planned maintenance isolation, emergency fault restoration, fault isolation, load transfer, construction support, or equipment testing.

attributes.name: outage_coordination_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this switching order requires coordination with the Outage Management System (OMS) for planned customer outage notifications. True indicates OMS coordination is required.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority classification for the switching order: emergency (immediate safety or reliability threat), high (critical infrastructure), medium (scheduled maintenance), or low (routine work).

attributes.name: reliability_impact_assessment
attributes.description: Documented assessment of the potential impact of this switching order on system reliability, including contingency analysis, N-1 criteria evaluation, and risk mitigation measures.

attributes.name: safety_clearance_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this switching order requires formal safety clearance and Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) procedures before execution. True indicates safety clearance is mandatory.
attributes.references: OSHA 1910.269 - Electric Power Generation, Transmission, and Distribution

attributes.name: scada_monitoring_enabled_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitoring Enabled Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether real-time SCADA monitoring and telemetry is enabled for the equipment and circuits affected by this switching order. True indicates SCADA monitoring is active.

attributes.name: scheduled_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when execution of this switching order is expected to be completed, including all steps and restoration.

attributes.name: scheduled_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time when execution of this switching order is scheduled to begin.

attributes.name: sequence_validation_status
attributes.description: Status of automated or manual validation of the switching step sequence for electrical safety, operational feasibility, and compliance with switching procedures: not validated, validated (passed all checks), validation failed (errors detected), or override approved (validation bypassed by authority).
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The operational system of record that originated this switching order data (e.g., GE PowerOn DMS/OMS, SCADA EMS).

attributes.name: switching_procedure_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the standard operating procedure (SOP) or switching instruction document that governs the execution of this switching order, including document number and version.

attributes.name: switching_step_count
attributes.description: The total number of discrete switching steps (individual device operations) defined in this switching order sequence.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn DMS/OMS Switching Order Module

attributes.name: voltage_class_kv
attributes.description: The nominal voltage class in kilovolts (kV) of the equipment and network segment affected by this switching order (e.g., 765, 500, 345, 230, 138, 69, 34.5, 13.8, 4.16 kV).

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Documented weather conditions at the time of switching order execution, relevant for safety assessment and operational decision-making (e.g., clear, rain, snow, high wind, lightning).

products.name: switching_step
products.description: Individual step within a switching order defining a single discrete switching action (open/close breaker, isolate section, ground equipment). Captures step sequence number, device identifier, action type, required safety tag, completion timestamp, and executing operator. Enables granular tracking of switching sequence execution and safety compliance.

attributes.name: switching_step_id
attributes.description: Unique system-generated identifier for each individual switching step record within the Databricks Silver Layer. Serves as the primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: authorizing_operator_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the control room operator or supervisor who authorized execution of this switching step. Supports two-person integrity requirements and chain-of-command compliance for high-voltage switching operations.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-005; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Each switching step is executed by a crew; linking enables tracking crew performance and safety compliance.

attributes.name: device_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific grid device (breaker, switch, disconnect, recloser, sectionalizer) on which this switching action is to be performed. Links to the asset registry in the Distribution Management System (DMS) or GIS.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; Esri ArcGIS; Maximo EAM

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the substation or switching station where the target device is physically located. Used for geographic and operational context in outage management and grid operations.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the operator or field technician who physically executed or confirmed execution of this switching step. Provides accountability and traceability for safety compliance and post-event analysis.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Reference to the distribution feeder circuit associated with the device being switched. Enables load flow analysis and outage impact assessment at the feeder level.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated outage event in the Outage Management System (OMS) that this switching step is part of restoring or isolating. Links switching activity to customer impact and SAIDI/SAIFI metrics.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: gridops_switching_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.gridops_switching_order. Business justification: Switching steps belong to an internal GridOps switching order; FK creates proper parent‑child link.

attributes.name: primary_switching_person_id
attributes.description: Reference to the operator or field technician who physically executed or confirmed execution of this switching step. Provides accountability and traceability for safety compliance and post-event analysis.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: The SCADA telemetry point identifier associated with the target device for this switching step. Used to retrieve real-time device status from the OSIsoft PI Historian or EMS/DMS SCADA system.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Maximo work order associated with the maintenance or construction activity that necessitated this switching step. Links switching operations to asset maintenance workflows.
attributes.references: Maximo EAM; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: The discrete switching action to be performed in this step. Defines the specific operation on the identified device: open or close a breaker/switch, apply or remove a ground, or isolate/energize a section of the grid.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; IEEE C37.100; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: actual_execution_timestamp
