attributes.description: The actual date and time at which this switching step was physically completed by the executing operator. Used for outage duration calculations, SAIDI/SAIFI reporting, and post-switching analysis.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: arc_flash_boundary_ft
attributes.description: The calculated arc flash protection boundary in feet for the device associated with this switching step, as determined by arc flash hazard analysis. Defines the minimum safe approach distance for personnel.

attributes.name: communication_method
attributes.description: The method used to communicate the switching instruction between the control room operator and the field operator for this step. Documents the communication channel for audit trail and NERC compliance purposes.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-005; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: confirmed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which the control room operator confirmed receipt of the completed step notification from the field operator. Captures the two-way communication verification required for safe switching operations.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this switching step record was first created in the system, typically when the switching order was drafted and steps were defined. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: critical_customer_impacted
attributes.description: Indicates whether this switching step affects one or more critical customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment facilities, or other life-safety accounts). Triggers priority restoration protocols and regulatory notification requirements.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; State PUC Reporting; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: customers_affected_count
attributes.description: The number of customer service points that are de-energized or affected as a direct result of this switching step. Used for outage impact assessment, SAIDI/SAIFI calculations, and customer notification prioritization.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; State PUC Reporting; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: deviation_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for any deviation from the planned switching step, such as a step being skipped, reordered, or modified during execution. Required for post-event review and regulatory compliance documentation.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-005; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: device_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label of the grid device targeted by this switching step, as maintained in the Distribution Management System (DMS) or GIS asset registry. Supports operator identification in the field.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: device_state_after
attributes.description: The verified state of the switching device immediately after this step was executed. Confirms the post-condition of the device and validates that the intended switching action was successfully completed.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: device_state_before
attributes.description: The verified state of the switching device immediately before this step was executed. Confirms the pre-condition of the device and supports post-event reconstruction of grid topology changes.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: device_type
attributes.description: Classification of the grid switching device targeted by this step. Indicates the physical type of apparatus to be operated, which determines the applicable operating procedure and safety requirements.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; IEEE C37.100; Esri ArcGIS

attributes.name: executing_operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the operator or field technician who executed this switching step. Captured at time of execution for audit trail and regulatory compliance purposes.

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: The unique feature identifier of the target device in the Esri ArcGIS geospatial asset management system. Enables spatial analysis, field crew navigation, and integration with the Distribution Management System (DMS) network model.
attributes.references: Esri ArcGIS; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this switching step record was most recently modified, such as when step status was updated, notes were added, or execution was confirmed. Supports change tracking and audit compliance.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: load_current_amps
attributes.description: The measured or estimated load current in amperes flowing through the device at the time of the switching step. Used to assess whether the switching operation is within the device's rated interrupting capacity.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; IEEE C37.100

attributes.name: network_model_node_code
attributes.description: The node identifier of the target device within the DMS/EMS network connectivity model. Used for power flow analysis, load flow calculations, and topology processing to validate switching step safety.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC FAC-002

attributes.name: ppe_required
attributes.description: Description of the minimum Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) required for safe execution of this switching step, such as arc flash suit rating, rubber gloves class, and face shield requirements per OSHA and NFPA 70E standards.

attributes.name: protective_relay_coordination
attributes.description: Indicates whether protective relay coordination checks are required before executing this switching step. Ensures that relay settings and protection schemes remain valid after the switching operation to prevent cascading failures.
attributes.references: NERC PRC-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; IEEE C37.100

attributes.name: remote_operation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this switching step was executed remotely from the control room via SCADA/DMS, as opposed to a manual field operation by a crew member. Distinguishes automated from manual switching for reliability analysis.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: repeat_back_verified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the field operator performed a verbal repeat-back of the switching instruction to the control room operator prior to execution, as required by NERC operating procedures for safe switching.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-005; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: safety_tag_number
attributes.description: The unique identifier of the safety tag (hold tag, caution tag, or danger tag) associated with this switching step. Required for lockout/tagout (LOTO) compliance tracking and personnel protection verification.

attributes.name: safety_tag_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether a safety tag (hold tag, caution tag, or danger tag) must be applied or verified before this switching step can be executed. Critical for personnel safety and OSHA compliance.

attributes.name: safety_tag_type
attributes.description: Classification of the safety tag associated with this switching step. Distinguishes between hold tags (prohibit operation), caution tags (warn of hazard), danger tags (imminent hazard), and clearance tags (work authorization).

attributes.name: scada_verified
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Verified Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the device state change for this switching step was independently verified by the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, providing automated confirmation beyond operator verbal report.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: scheduled_execution_timestamp
attributes.description: The planned date and time at which this switching step is scheduled to be executed, as defined in the approved switching order. Used for outage coordination and crew scheduling.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: source_system_step_reference
attributes.description: The native identifier of this switching step record in the originating operational system (GE PowerOn DMS/OMS). Preserves the source system key for data lineage, reconciliation, and cross-system traceability in the Silver Layer.

attributes.name: step_instruction
attributes.description: Detailed written instruction describing the exact action to be performed in this switching step, including device location, access method, and any special precautions. Provides the field operator with unambiguous direction.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: step_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operator notes, observations, or deviations recorded at the time of step execution. Captures field conditions, anomalies, or explanations for skipped or failed steps.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: step_number
attributes.description: Sequential position of this switching step within the parent switching order. Defines the mandatory execution order of discrete switching actions to ensure safe and correct grid reconfiguration.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC FAC-001; IEEE C37.100

attributes.name: step_status
attributes.description: Current execution lifecycle state of this individual switching step. Tracks whether the step is awaiting execution, actively being performed, successfully completed, skipped per approved deviation, failed, or cancelled.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: step_type
attributes.description: Classifies the nature of this switching step within the overall switching plan. Primary steps are the core switching actions; contingency steps are alternatives; restoration steps return the grid to normal; verification steps confirm device state; notification steps record required communications.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: switching_purpose
attributes.description: The operational reason or purpose for which this switching step is being performed. Classifies the switching activity to support reliability reporting, outage analysis, and regulatory compliance categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned_maintenance|emergency_restoration|load_transfer|fault_isolation|construction|testing — promote to reference product if additional values are needed]
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-005; State PUC Reporting

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: The nominal operating voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the circuit or equipment associated with this switching step. Determines the applicable safety clearance distances, PPE requirements, and operating procedures.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; NERC FAC-001; IEEE C37.100

products.name: gridops_outage_event
products.description: Master record for each grid outage event managed through the OMS (GE PowerOn), encompassing the full outage lifecycle from detection through restoration. Header captures outage type (planned/unplanned/momentary), affected network segment, cause code (IEEE 1366), estimated and confirmed customers affected, start timestamp, ETR (estimated time of restoration), and regulatory notification status. Includes a chronological restoration log tracking each milestone (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching action, partial restoration, full restoration) with timestamps, restored customer counts, restoration method, and responsible crew. Serves as the SSOT for outage lifecycle management, SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI/MAIFI calculation, regulatory reporting (state PUC, DOE OE-417), and post-storm analysis.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the grid outage event record. Primary key for the outage event entity in the Outage Management System (OMS).

attributes.name: asset_registry_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Required for Outage Management Report: each outage event must identify the primary asset that caused the failure for regulatory reporting and restoration planning.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Outage events are scoped to a balancing area; FK provides relational integrity.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Supports Outage Cost Recovery and regulatory reporting by assigning outage events to a cost center.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.crew. Business justification: Outage Management assigns a primary crew responsible for restoration; needed for outage restoration reporting.

attributes.name: filing_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.filing. Business justification: Regulatory outage reporting filing (e.g., FERC Form 1) requires linking each outage event to its filing for compliance.

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.incident. Business justification: Regulatory outage report requires linking each outage event to a safety incident for compliance and root‑cause analysis.

attributes.name: incident_ticket_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to technology.incident_ticket. Business justification: Outage events generate IT incident tickets for system issues; linking enables root‑cause tracking and IT service level compliance.

attributes.name: purchase_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.purchase_order. Business justification: Repair work after an outage is often funded by a purchase order; linking supports restoration cost reporting and budgeting.

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the specific equipment asset that failed. Links to Maximo EAM for asset history, maintenance records, and replacement tracking.

attributes.name: resource_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to der.der_resource. Business justification: Outage management tracks which DER resources are impacted to coordinate restoration and reliability reporting.

attributes.name: storm_event_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.storm_event. Business justification: Storm‑caused outages must be linked to the originating storm event for emergency response coordination and reporting.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Outage restoration contracts external vendors; reporting (FERC/NERC) mandates identifying the vendor responsible for each outage event.

attributes.name: affected_feeder_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the distribution feeder (primary circuit) affected by the outage. Critical for outage location, crew dispatch, and reliability metric calculation by feeder.

attributes.name: affected_substation_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the substation serving the affected network segment. Used for outage aggregation, crew routing, and asset management coordination.

attributes.name: alarm_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Alarm ID
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA alarm that triggered or correlated with this outage event. Links to PI Historian and EMS for real-time operational data and root cause analysis. Also known as SCADA alarm ID.

attributes.name: confirmed_customers_affected
attributes.description: Final confirmed count of customer accounts that experienced a service interruption during this outage event. Used for official SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, and MAIFI calculations and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this outage event record was first created in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change tracking.

attributes.name: crew_arrival_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crews arrived on-site at the outage location. Used to calculate travel time and time-to-repair metrics.

attributes.name: crew_dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when field crews were dispatched to investigate and restore the outage. Used to calculate response time metrics and crew utilization.

attributes.name: critical_infrastructure_affected_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether the outage affected critical infrastructure customers (hospitals, emergency services, water treatment, communications). Triggers priority restoration and regulatory notification.

attributes.name: customer_minutes_interrupted
attributes.description: Total customer-minutes of interruption, calculated as the sum of (customers affected × duration) for each restoration milestone. Primary input for SAIDI calculation. Also known as CMI.

attributes.name: equipment_failed_type
attributes.description: Type of equipment that failed and caused the outage (e.g., transformer, recloser, fuse, conductor, insulator, switch). Links to asset management for failure analysis and replacement planning.

attributes.name: estimated_customers_affected
attributes.description: Initial estimate of the number of customer accounts affected by the outage, typically calculated by the OMS based on network topology and meter connectivity. Updated as outage scope is refined.

attributes.name: estimated_restoration_time
attributes.description: The estimated date and time when service is expected to be fully restored. Communicated to customers and updated as restoration progresses. Also known as ETR.

attributes.name: fault_isolation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the fault was successfully isolated from the rest of the network through switching operations. Enables partial restoration to unaffected customers.

attributes.name: first_restoration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when service was first restored to any subset of affected customers, typically through switching operations or temporary measures.

attributes.name: major_event_day_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this outage occurred during a Major Event Day as defined by IEEE 1366 2.5 beta method. MED outages are typically excluded from reliability metric calculations. Also known as MED flag.

attributes.name: oms_external_reference
attributes.description: External identifier from the source OMS system (GE PowerOn). Used for cross-system reconciliation and data lineage tracking. Also known as OMS external ID.

attributes.name: oms_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source OMS system that created this outage record (e.g., GE PowerOn, Oracle OMS). Used for data lineage and multi-system integration scenarios. Also known as OMS source system.

attributes.name: outage_cause_code
attributes.description: Standardized IEEE 1366 cause code identifying the root cause of the outage (e.g., equipment failure, tree contact, animal contact, weather, vehicle accident, planned maintenance).

attributes.name: outage_cause_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the outage cause, including specific circumstances, equipment involved, and contributing factors. Captured by field crews during restoration.

attributes.name: outage_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Total duration of the outage event in minutes, calculated as the difference between outage start and end timestamps. Used for SAIDI and CAIDI reliability metric calculations.

attributes.name: outage_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when service was fully restored to all affected customers. Used to calculate total outage duration for reliability metrics and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: outage_location_address
attributes.description: Street address or nearest intersection to the outage location. Used for crew dispatch, customer communication, and regulatory reporting. Organizational contact data classified as confidential.

attributes.name: outage_location_latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the outage location in decimal degrees. Used for crew routing, GIS mapping, and spatial analysis of outage patterns.

attributes.name: outage_location_longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the outage location in decimal degrees. Used for crew routing, GIS mapping, and spatial analysis of outage patterns.

attributes.name: outage_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the outage event, typically generated by the OMS (GE PowerOn). Used for external communication, crew dispatch, and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: outage_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the outage event was first detected or reported. This is the official start time used for SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI, and MAIFI reliability metric calculations.

attributes.name: outage_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the outage event. Tracks progression from initial detection through crew dispatch, fault isolation, restoration activities, and final closure. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: detected|confirmed|dispatched|isolated|restoring|restored|closed — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: outage_type
attributes.description: Classification of the outage event. Planned outages are scheduled maintenance; unplanned are unexpected interruptions; momentary are brief interruptions typically under 5 minutes.

attributes.name: peak_customers_out
attributes.description: Maximum number of customers simultaneously without service at any point during the outage event. Used for storm impact assessment and resource planning.

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator whether this outage event requires notification to regulatory authorities (state PUC, FERC, DOE) based on customer count, duration, or critical infrastructure impact thresholds.
attributes.references: DOE OE-417 Electric Emergency Incident Reporting

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when regulatory notification was submitted to the appropriate authority (state PUC, FERC, DOE). Required for compliance audit trail.
attributes.references: DOE OE-417 Electric Emergency Incident Reporting

attributes.name: restoration_method
attributes.description: Primary method used to restore service (e.g., switching, repair, replacement, temporary bypass, mobile substation). Used for restoration strategy analysis and resource planning.

attributes.name: storm_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the storm event if this outage was part of a named storm (e.g., Hurricane Ida, Winter Storm Uri). Used for storm impact analysis and FEMA reporting.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this outage event record was last modified in the data platform. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and change tracking.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather conditions at the time of the outage event (e.g., clear, rain, snow, ice, wind, lightning, hurricane, tornado). Used for cause analysis and major event day (MED) classification.

products.name: outage_restoration_log
products.description: Detailed chronological log of restoration activities for each outage event, capturing each restoration milestone (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching action, partial restoration, full restoration). Records timestamp, restored customer count, restoration method, and responsible crew. Supports CAIDI calculation, regulatory reporting, and post-storm analysis.

attributes.name: outage_restoration_log_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each restoration activity log entry. Primary key for the outage restoration log.

attributes.name: crew_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the field crew responsible for this restoration activity. Links to workforce management system for crew performance analysis.

attributes.name: distribution_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the substation associated with this restoration activity. Supports substation-level restoration performance analysis.

attributes.name: feeder_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the distribution feeder affected by this restoration activity. Links to distribution network model for circuit-level analysis.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent outage event that this restoration activity belongs to. Links restoration activities to the originating outage.

attributes.name: automated_restoration_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this restoration was performed automatically by distribution automation systems. True if automated, false if manual crew intervention was required.

attributes.name: cause_code
attributes.description: Standardized code identifying the root cause of the outage being restored. Links to cause code reference table for regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: crew_type
attributes.description: Classification of crew performing the restoration work. Distinguishes between internal utility crews, contractors, mutual aid crews, and emergency response teams.

attributes.name: customer_callback_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether customer callbacks are required after this restoration milestone. True if customers need to be contacted to verify service restoration.

attributes.name: customers_restored_count
attributes.description: Number of customers whose service was restored at this milestone. Used for calculating cumulative restoration progress and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: data_source_system
attributes.description: Name of the source system that provided this restoration log data (e.g., OMS, DMS, SCADA, field mobile application). Supports data lineage and integration troubleshooting.

attributes.name: device_location
attributes.description: Physical location or address of the device operated during restoration. Enables geographic analysis of restoration activities.

attributes.name: device_operated
attributes.description: Identifier or name of the electrical device operated during this restoration milestone (e.g., circuit breaker, recloser, switch). Supports asset performance analysis.

attributes.name: dms_event_code
attributes.description: Reference identifier from the Distribution Management System for this restoration event. Links to DMS for advanced distribution automation analysis.

attributes.name: equipment_failure_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether equipment failure was identified during this restoration activity. True if equipment failure was discovered, false otherwise.

attributes.name: estimated_restoration_time
attributes.description: Estimated time when restoration was expected to be completed at the time this milestone was logged. Used for comparing actual vs. estimated restoration performance.

attributes.name: load_restored_mw
attributes.description: Amount of electrical load in megawatts restored at this milestone. Supports grid operations analysis and capacity restoration tracking.

attributes.name: mutual_aid_request_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether mutual aid resources were requested or utilized for this restoration activity. True if mutual aid was involved, false otherwise.

attributes.name: oms_ticket_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the OMS trouble ticket associated with this restoration activity. Links to outage management system for end-to-end outage tracking.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Priority classification assigned to this restoration activity. Critical facilities (hospitals, emergency services) receive higher priority.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this restoration log record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage and audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this restoration log record was last modified. Tracks data currency and supports audit trail requirements.

attributes.name: restoration_cost_estimate
attributes.description: Estimated cost in USD associated with this restoration activity. Includes labor, materials, and equipment costs for financial tracking and storm cost analysis.

attributes.name: restoration_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration in minutes from outage start to this restoration milestone. Used for calculating CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index) and other reliability metrics.

attributes.name: restoration_method
attributes.description: Method used to restore service at this milestone. Indicates whether restoration was via primary feed, alternate feed, temporary generation, or switching operations.

attributes.name: restoration_milestone_type
attributes.description: Classification of the restoration activity milestone. Defines the type of restoration event being logged (crew dispatch, fault isolation, switching, partial or full restoration).

attributes.name: restoration_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes and observations recorded by field crews during restoration activity. Captures operational details, challenges encountered, and lessons learned.

attributes.name: restoration_sequence_number
attributes.description: Sequential ordering of restoration activities within a single outage event. Enables chronological reconstruction of restoration workflow.

attributes.name: restoration_status
attributes.description: Current status of this restoration activity. Tracks whether the restoration milestone is in progress, completed, failed, or pending verification.

attributes.name: restoration_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this specific restoration milestone occurred. Critical for calculating restoration duration metrics and CAIDI (Customer Average Interruption Duration Index).

attributes.name: safety_incident_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a safety incident occurred during this restoration activity. True if any safety event was reported, false otherwise.

attributes.name: scada_confirmation_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Confirmation Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the restoration activity was confirmed via SCADA system. True if SCADA telemetry verified the restoration, false if manual confirmation only.
attributes.references: NERC CIP Standards, NIST Smart Grid Framework

attributes.name: switching_order_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the switching order executed during this restoration activity. Links to switching order management system for operational traceability.

attributes.name: vegetation_related_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether vegetation contact or interference was involved in the outage being restored. True if vegetation-related, false otherwise.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather conditions present during this restoration activity. Supports correlation analysis between weather and restoration performance.

products.name: reliability_event
products.description: Records NERC-reportable and internally tracked reliability events including disturbances, contingencies, N-1 violations, BES incidents, and all associated operator log entries and control room communications. Each event captures classification per NERC EOP/TOP standards, affected facilities, initiating cause, system impact (MW lost, customers affected), regulatory reporting obligation, and timeline. Includes chronological operator actions, observations, shift handoff notes, alarm acknowledgments, inter-utility communications, and free-text narratives forming the complete operational record. Also serves as the repository for routine operator log entries (shift logs, standing orders, equipment status notes) classified by entry type. Feeds NERC OE-417, state PUC disturbance reporting, NERC CIP compliance evidence, and serves as the official auditable operational record for all control room activities.

attributes.name: reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the reliability event record. Primary key for the reliability event entity.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Reliability events are associated with a balancing area; FK replaces free‑text field.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reliability event to associated customer outage records in the Outage Management System. Used for cross-system correlation and customer impact analysis.

attributes.name: incident_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.incident. Business justification: Major reliability events trigger safety incident investigations for regulatory reporting and corrective action.

attributes.name: oms_outage_gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier linking this reliability event to associated customer outage records in the Outage Management System. Used for cross-system correlation and customer impact analysis.

attributes.name: affected_facilities
attributes.description: List or description of transmission lines, substations, generation units, or other Bulk Electric System (BES) facilities impacted by the reliability event. Includes facility identifiers and equipment names.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-004 Event Reporting Standard, NERC CIP-002

attributes.name: analysis_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when the post-event analysis or root cause investigation was completed. Null if analysis is not yet complete or not required.

attributes.name: caidi_impact_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Customer Average Interruption Duration Index (CAIDI) Impact Minutes
attributes.description: Contribution of this reliability event to the utility's CAIDI metric, measured in average minutes per customer interruption. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: cip_incident_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this reliability event is also classified as a NERC CIP cyber security or physical security incident requiring separate CIP incident reporting. True if CIP incident reporting is required.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-008 Incident Reporting and Response Planning

attributes.name: contributing_factors
attributes.description: Additional factors that contributed to the severity or propagation of the reliability event. May include cascading failures, inadequate operating reserves, communication failures, or procedural gaps.

attributes.name: control_room_location
attributes.description: Physical location or identifier of the control room where the reliability event was managed. Used for tracking operational responsibility and shift coordination.

attributes.name: corrective_actions_taken
attributes.description: Description of immediate corrective actions taken by operators to mitigate or resolve the reliability event. Includes switching operations, load shedding, generation dispatch adjustments, and emergency procedures executed.

attributes.name: customers_affected
attributes.description: Total number of customer accounts that experienced service interruption as a result of the reliability event. Used for outage impact assessment and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-004, State PUC Reporting Requirements

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reliability event was first detected by control room operators, SCADA alarms, or automated monitoring systems. May differ from event start if detection was delayed.

attributes.name: ems_case_code
attributes.description: Identifier for the EMS state estimator case or snapshot associated with the reliability event. Links to power flow analysis and system state data at the time of the event.

attributes.name: estimated_restoration_timestamp
attributes.description: Estimated date and time when full service restoration is expected to be completed. Updated as restoration work progresses. Null if event is already resolved.

attributes.name: event_classification
attributes.description: Primary classification of the reliability event per NERC EOP/TOP standards and internal utility categorization. Determines regulatory reporting obligations and escalation procedures.

attributes.name: event_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the reliability event was fully resolved and normal operations restored. Null if event is still ongoing. Used to calculate event duration.

attributes.name: event_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique identifier for the reliability event, used in regulatory reporting and inter-utility communications. Typically follows utility-specific or NERC-prescribed numbering conventions.

attributes.name: event_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the reliability event was first detected or initiated. Represents the beginning of the disturbance or incident. Critical for NERC timeline reporting.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the reliability event. Tracks progression from initial detection through investigation, containment, resolution, and final closure.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Detailed type of reliability event such as transmission outage, generation loss, voltage deviation, frequency excursion, load shed, protective relay operation, or equipment failure. Provides granular categorization beyond classification.

attributes.name: frequency_deviation_hz
attributes.description: Maximum frequency deviation from nominal 60 Hz (or 50 Hz) observed during the reliability event. Measured in Hertz. Critical for assessing system stability and NERC BAL standard compliance.

attributes.name: initiating_cause
attributes.description: Root cause or triggering event that initiated the reliability event. Examples include equipment failure, weather event, human error, cyber incident, protective relay misoperation, or external disturbance.

attributes.name: lessons_learned
attributes.description: Summary of key lessons learned from the reliability event. Includes insights on operational procedures, equipment performance, communication effectiveness, and recommendations for improvement.

attributes.name: mw_generation_lost
attributes.description: Total amount of generation capacity lost during the reliability event, measured in megawatts. Includes forced outages and emergency shutdowns of generation units.

attributes.name: mw_load_lost
attributes.description: Total amount of customer load lost during the reliability event, measured in megawatts. Key metric for assessing event severity and NERC reporting thresholds.

attributes.name: nerc_oe417_report_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) OE-417 Report ID
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the NERC OE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report filed for this reliability event. Links to official regulatory submission.

attributes.name: nerc_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event meets NERC criteria for mandatory reporting under EOP-004 or other NERC standards. True if event must be reported to NERC.

attributes.name: notification_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the reliability event was formally notified to NERC, RTO/ISO, state PUC, or other regulatory authorities. Critical for compliance with reporting deadlines.

attributes.name: operator_entry_type
attributes.description: Classification of the operator log entry by type. Distinguishes between event-related actions, routine observations, shift logs, standing orders, and equipment status notes. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: event_action|observation|communication|shift_handoff|alarm_ack|switching_order|standing_order|equipment_status — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: operator_log_entry
attributes.description: Chronological free-text narrative of operator actions, observations, and communications during the reliability event. Includes shift handoff notes, alarm acknowledgments, switching orders executed, and inter-utility communications. Forms the official auditable operational record.

attributes.name: operator_name
attributes.description: Name of the control room operator who logged the entry or took action during the reliability event. Used for operational accountability and training purposes.

attributes.name: post_event_analysis_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a formal post-event analysis or root cause investigation is required for this reliability event. True for significant events requiring detailed technical review.

attributes.name: preventive_actions_recommended
attributes.description: Recommended preventive actions to avoid recurrence of similar reliability events. May include equipment upgrades, procedure changes, training enhancements, or system reinforcements.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this reliability event record was last modified. Updated whenever any field in the record changes. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: restoration_priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned for service restoration efforts. Critical priority for hospitals, emergency services, and critical infrastructure; high for large customer groups; medium and low for routine restoration.

attributes.name: rto_iso_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Region
attributes.description: RTO or ISO region where the reliability event occurred. Examples include PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE. Used for regional coordination and reporting.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2000, NERC Regional Entity Standards

attributes.name: saidi_impact_minutes
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Impact Minutes
attributes.description: Contribution of this reliability event to the utility's SAIDI metric, measured in customer-minutes of interruption. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: saifi_impact_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Impact Count
attributes.description: Contribution of this reliability event to the utility's SAIFI metric, measured as interruption frequency per customer. Used for reliability performance tracking and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: scada_alarm_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Alarm Count
attributes.description: Total number of SCADA alarms triggered during the reliability event. Used to assess event complexity and operator workload during the incident.

attributes.name: shift_supervisor_name
attributes.description: Name of the shift supervisor on duty during the reliability event. Used for operational accountability and post-event review coordination.

attributes.name: state_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this event must be reported to state Public Utility Commission per state-specific disturbance reporting requirements. True if state reporting is required.

attributes.name: voltage_deviation_kv
attributes.description: Maximum voltage deviation from normal operating range observed during the reliability event. Measured in kilovolts. Used to assess voltage stability and equipment stress.

attributes.name: weather_conditions
attributes.description: Description of weather conditions at the time of the reliability event. Includes temperature, wind speed, precipitation, lightning activity, and other relevant meteorological data.

attributes.name: weather_related_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the reliability event was caused or significantly influenced by weather conditions such as storms, lightning, ice, wind, or extreme temperatures. True if weather was a factor.

products.name: dr_dispatch_event
products.description: Records each demand response (DR) dispatch event issued by grid operations to enrolled DR resources and aggregators, with full per-resource performance tracking. Header captures dispatch trigger (emergency, economic, capacity, test), target MW reduction, dispatch window, notification method, and overall program compliance status. Detail records capture each participating resource's identifier, resource type, nominated MW reduction, actual metered MW reduction (from interval meter data), response time, ramp compliance, performance score, and settlement-ready compliance flag. Integrates with DERMS for DER-based DR and with the product domain for DR program definitions. Supports DR capacity payment settlement, program compliance verification, FERC Order 2222 reporting, and resource performance trending.
products.reference: DERMS DR Dispatch / Demand Response Event

attributes.name: dr_dispatch_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the demand response dispatch event. Primary key.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: DR dispatch events are executed within a balancing area; FK adds referential integrity.

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.compliance_obligation. Business justification: Demand‑Response dispatches must satisfy a documented compliance obligation; the FK ties each dispatch to its obligation record.

attributes.name: customer_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: DR Dispatch Report requires linking each dispatch to the customer account enrolled in the program for settlement and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: der_program_id

attributes.name: dr_enrollment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.dr_enrollment. Business justification: Compliance audit tracks which specific DR enrollment was dispatched; the DR dispatch event must reference the enrollment record.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the grid operations control room operator who issued the DR dispatch event.
attributes.references: EMS Operator Registry, NERC Personnel Certification

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the outage management system (OMS) event that triggered this DR dispatch, if the dispatch was issued in response to a grid outage or contingency.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.description: The identifier of the grid operations control room operator who issued the DR dispatch event.
attributes.references: EMS Operator Registry, NERC Personnel Certification

attributes.name: product_program_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.product_program. Business justification: DR dispatch events are executed under a specific demand‑response program defined in product_program; required for program performance tracking.

attributes.name: wbs_element_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.wbs_element. Business justification: Demand‑Response dispatches are tracked as projects; linking to WBS enables budgeting and cost tracking.

attributes.name: actual_mw_reduction
attributes.description: The actual measured load reduction in megawatts (MW) achieved across all participating resources, aggregated from interval meter data.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_f
attributes.description: The ambient outdoor temperature in degrees Fahrenheit at the time of dispatch, used for weather normalization and performance analysis.
attributes.references: NOAA Weather Data, ISO/RTO Weather Stations

attributes.name: baseline_methodology
attributes.description: The baseline calculation methodology used to determine pre-event load and measure actual reduction: high 10 of 10 (highest 10 of last 10 similar days), mid 8 of 10, high 5 of 10, customer baseline (negotiated), or meter before/after (direct measurement).

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Overall program compliance status for this dispatch event: compliant (met all requirements), non-compliant (failed to meet targets), partial (some resources complied), under review (pending settlement), exempt (test or waived event).
attributes.references: DR Program Compliance Rules, FERC Order 745

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this DR dispatch event record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: derms_integration_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) Integration Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dispatch event was coordinated through the DERMS platform for DER-based DR resources.

attributes.name: dispatch_authorization_code
attributes.description: The authorization code or approval reference for the dispatch event, required for emergency and economic dispatches per operating procedures.

attributes.name: dispatch_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The total duration of the DR dispatch event in minutes, calculated from start to end timestamp.

attributes.name: dispatch_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The scheduled end date and time for the DR curtailment event.

attributes.name: dispatch_issued_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the DR dispatch event was issued by grid operations to participating resources.

attributes.name: dispatch_notes
attributes.description: Free-text operational notes and comments recorded by the dispatch operator regarding event circumstances, special conditions, or post-event observations.

attributes.name: dispatch_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the DR dispatch event, formatted as DR-YYYYMMDD-NNNN for external reference and operational tracking.

attributes.name: dispatch_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The scheduled start date and time for the DR curtailment event.

attributes.name: dispatch_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the DR dispatch event: pending (notification sent, not yet active), active (curtailment in progress), completed (event concluded), cancelled (event aborted), failed (dispatch unsuccessful).

attributes.name: dispatch_trigger_type
attributes.description: The operational reason for issuing the DR dispatch: emergency (grid emergency), economic (price-driven), capacity (resource adequacy), test (program validation), scheduled (planned event), or reliability (NERC compliance).
attributes.references: NERC EOP Standards, ISO/RTO Operating Procedures

attributes.name: ferc_2222_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Order 2222 Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this dispatch event involves aggregated DER participation and is reportable under FERC Order 2222 requirements.

attributes.name: frequency_deviation_hz
attributes.description: The grid frequency deviation in hertz (Hz) from nominal 60 Hz at the time of dispatch, if the dispatch was triggered by frequency regulation needs.
attributes.references: NERC BAL Standards, SCADA Frequency Monitoring

attributes.name: grid_emergency_level
attributes.description: The grid emergency alert level at the time of dispatch issuance, ranging from normal to emergency levels 1-3 per NERC EEA protocols.

attributes.name: iso_rto_market
attributes.business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) / Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Market
attributes.description: The ISO or RTO market jurisdiction under which this DR dispatch was executed. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PJM|CAISO|ERCOT|MISO|NYISO|ISO-NE|SPP|non-ISO — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this DR dispatch event record was last updated, reflecting status changes, performance data updates, or settlement finalization.

attributes.name: lmp_trigger_price
attributes.description: The locational marginal price (LMP) in dollars per MWh that triggered an economic DR dispatch, if applicable.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Day-Ahead and Real-Time Market Pricing

attributes.name: notification_lead_time_minutes
attributes.description: The advance notice time in minutes between dispatch issuance and dispatch start, as required by program rules.

attributes.name: notification_method
attributes.description: The primary method used to notify DR participants of the dispatch event: automated signal (OpenADR, API), phone, email, SMS, web portal, or SCADA command.

attributes.name: performance_percentage
attributes.description: The overall performance of the dispatch event expressed as a percentage of actual MW reduction divided by target MW reduction.

attributes.name: scada_snapshot_timestamp
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Snapshot Timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp of the SCADA system snapshot captured at dispatch issuance, used for grid state verification and post-event analysis.

attributes.name: settlement_amount
attributes.description: The total financial settlement amount in USD to be paid to all participating DR resources for this dispatch event, based on performance and program rates.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Tariff, DR Program Payment Terms

attributes.name: settlement_ready_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether all performance data has been validated and the event is ready for financial settlement and capacity payment processing.

attributes.name: target_mw_reduction
attributes.description: The total target load reduction in megawatts (MW) requested from all participating DR resources for this dispatch event.

attributes.name: total_resources_dispatched
attributes.description: The total count of individual DR resources (customers, aggregators, DERs) that were dispatched as part of this event.

attributes.name: total_resources_responded
attributes.description: The count of dispatched resources that successfully responded and achieved measurable load reduction during the event.

attributes.name: voltage_deviation_kv
attributes.description: The voltage deviation in kilovolts (kV) from nominal levels at critical substations, if the dispatch was triggered by voltage control needs.
attributes.references: NERC VAR Standards, SCADA Voltage Monitoring

attributes.name: weather_adjusted_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the baseline and performance calculations were adjusted for weather conditions (temperature, humidity) per program rules.

products.name: dr_resource_response
products.description: Captures the measured performance response of each individual DR resource or aggregator to a specific DR dispatch event. Records resource identifier, nominated MW reduction, actual metered MW reduction, response time, compliance flag, and performance score. Used for DR settlement, program compliance verification, and resource performance tracking.

attributes.name: dr_resource_response_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the demand response resource response record. Primary key.

attributes.name: aggregator_id
attributes.description: Reference to the aggregator entity if this resource is part of an aggregated DR portfolio.

attributes.name: dr_dispatch_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to the parent DR dispatch event that triggered this resource response.

attributes.name: dr_resource_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific DR resource or aggregator that responded to the dispatch event.

attributes.name: product_program_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific DR program under which this response was dispatched.

attributes.name: actual_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The actual duration in minutes that the resource sustained the load reduction.

attributes.name: actual_load_mw
attributes.description: The actual metered load in megawatts during the DR event period, measured from AMI or SCADA systems.

attributes.name: actual_reduction_mw
attributes.description: The actual measured load reduction in megawatts achieved by the resource, calculated as baseline minus actual load.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, ISO/RTO DR Settlement Standards

attributes.name: balancing_authority_area
attributes.description: The balancing authority area code where this DR resource is located and responded.

attributes.name: baseline_calculation_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to calculate the baseline load for this resource (e.g., 10-of-10, 5-of-10, regression-based).

attributes.name: baseline_load_mw
attributes.description: The calculated baseline load in megawatts representing what the resource would have consumed without the DR event, used for settlement calculations.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO Baseline Calculation Methodologies, FERC Order 745

attributes.name: compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the resource met the minimum performance requirements for the DR event (True = compliant, False = non-compliant).
attributes.references: ISO/RTO DR Compliance Rules, FERC Order 745

attributes.name: compliance_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage of nominated reduction actually delivered, calculated as (actual reduction / nominated reduction) * 100.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this resource response record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: dispatch_instruction_type
attributes.description: Classification of the dispatch instruction that triggered this response.

attributes.name: dispatch_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the DR dispatch signal was issued to the resource.

attributes.name: event_duration_minutes
attributes.description: The total duration in minutes that the resource was expected to maintain the load reduction.

attributes.name: meter_data_source
attributes.description: The source system or method used to capture the actual load measurements for this response.
attributes.references: MDM Standards, NERC Data Quality Standards

attributes.name: nominated_reduction_mw
attributes.description: The committed or nominated load reduction in megawatts that the resource agreed to provide for this dispatch event.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, ISO/RTO DR Settlement Standards

attributes.name: non_compliance_reason
attributes.description: Explanation or code indicating why the resource failed to meet compliance requirements, if applicable.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, exceptions, or additional context regarding this resource response.

attributes.name: penalty_amount_usd
attributes.description: Financial penalty assessed against the resource for non-compliance or under-performance, if applicable.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO DR Penalty Structures, FERC Standards

attributes.name: performance_score
attributes.description: Calculated performance score for the resource response, incorporating reduction accuracy, response time, and sustained performance. Used for resource ranking and future dispatch prioritization.

attributes.name: rebound_effect_mw
attributes.description: The measured load increase in megawatts immediately following the DR event, representing the rebound or snapback effect.

attributes.name: reduction_variance_mw
attributes.description: The difference between nominated and actual reduction in megawatts, used for compliance and performance assessment.

attributes.name: resource_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or identifier of the DR resource or aggregator for operational reference.

attributes.name: resource_type
