attributes.name: response_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the resource completed its response to the dispatch event.

attributes.name: response_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The actual date and time when the resource began responding to the dispatch signal.

attributes.name: response_time_minutes
attributes.description: The elapsed time in minutes from dispatch signal to the start of measurable load reduction, indicating resource responsiveness.
attributes.references: ISO/RTO DR Program Requirements, NERC Standards

attributes.name: settlement_amount_usd
attributes.description: The calculated payment amount in US dollars owed to the resource for its DR performance in this event, based on contracted rates and actual reduction.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, ISO/RTO DR Settlement Protocols

attributes.name: settlement_status
attributes.description: Current status of the financial settlement process for this resource response.

attributes.name: telemetry_quality_flag
attributes.description: Data quality indicator for the metered telemetry used in this response measurement.
attributes.references: NERC Data Quality Standards, MDM Best Practices

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this resource response record was last modified.
attributes.references: Data Governance Standards, Audit Trail Requirements

attributes.name: verification_method
attributes.description: The method used to verify and validate the resource response performance.

attributes.name: weather_adjustment_applied
attributes.description: Indicates whether a weather-based adjustment was applied to the baseline calculation to account for temperature or other weather impacts.

products.name: grid_contingency
products.description: Defines credible contingency scenarios (N-1, N-2, N-1-1) and stores all real-time and study-mode security assessment results performed by the EMS. Master contingency records specify contingency name, element(s) removed, contingency type, probability, monitoring elements, thermal and voltage limits, and active/inactive status in real-time security assessment. Assessment result records capture study timestamp, study type (real-time, day-ahead, planning), base case power flow results, number of violations found, worst-case contingency ranking, thermal overload details, voltage violation details, stability margin, and recommended corrective actions (redispatch, switching, load shed). Supports NERC TPL-001 through TPL-004, FAC-001/FAC-002 reliability standards, operator situational awareness, and real-time reliability compliance.

attributes.name: grid_contingency_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the grid contingency scenario record. Primary key for the grid contingency data product.
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001-5 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

attributes.name: scada_system_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System Identifier
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA system that provides real-time telemetry data for the elements involved in this contingency scenario.

attributes.name: balancing_area_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the balancing area or balancing authority area where this contingency is defined and monitored, used for jurisdictional and operational coordination.

attributes.name: cascading_outage_risk
attributes.description: Assessment of the risk that this contingency could trigger cascading outages affecting a wider area of the Bulk Electric System (BES), based on system topology, protection schemes, and historical events.

attributes.name: contingency_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Transmission Planning (TPL) Contingency Category
attributes.description: NERC TPL planning category classification: P0 (no contingency/base case), P1 (single element), P2 (single element with stuck breaker), P3 (loss of generator), P4 (multiple elements), P5 (delayed fault clearing), P6 (system instability), P7 (common structure). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: P0|P1|P2|P3|P4|P5|P6|P7 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: contingency_code
attributes.description: Unique business identifier or code used to reference this contingency in operational systems, study reports, and inter-system communication.

attributes.name: contingency_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or label assigned to this contingency scenario for operator identification and reference in Energy Management System (EMS) displays and reports.

attributes.name: contingency_type
attributes.description: Classification of the contingency scenario based on the number and type of elements removed. N-1 represents single element outage, N-2 represents simultaneous loss of two elements, N-1-1 represents sequential loss of two elements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: N-1|N-2|N-1-1|generator_trip|line_trip|transformer_trip|bus_fault|multiple_element — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: NERC TPL-001-5 Category P1 through P7

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether corrective actions (generation redispatch, transmission switching, load shedding) are required to maintain system reliability if this contingency occurs.

attributes.name: corrective_action_time_minutes
attributes.description: Maximum time in minutes allowed to implement corrective actions after this contingency occurs, based on thermal time constants, voltage decay rates, and operational procedures.

attributes.name: corrective_action_type
attributes.description: Type of corrective action recommended or required to mitigate violations resulting from this contingency. May include multiple actions separated by semicolons (e.g., 'generation redispatch; transmission switching').

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contingency record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.

attributes.name: dms_zone_code
attributes.description: Identifier linking this contingency to the DMS zone for transmission-distribution coordination and voltage control at the interface.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this contingency definition became active and was included in security assessment processes.

attributes.name: elements_removed_count
attributes.business_glossary_term: Number of Elements Removed in Contingency
attributes.description: Count of transmission or generation elements (lines, transformers, generators, buses) that are removed or tripped in this contingency scenario definition.

attributes.name: ems_system_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the EMS system instance where this contingency definition is maintained and where real-time security assessments are executed.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this contingency definition expires or is scheduled to be removed from active security assessment, typically due to system topology changes or element retirement. Null for indefinite contingencies.

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: Geographic region or sub-region identifier for this contingency, used for regional reliability coordination and reporting.

attributes.name: grid_contingency_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the contingency scenario in the real-time security assessment engine. Active contingencies are monitored continuously; inactive contingencies are excluded from real-time analysis.

attributes.name: interconnection_type
attributes.description: North American power grid interconnection where this contingency is located: Eastern Interconnection, Western Interconnection, Texas Interconnection (ERCOT), or Quebec Interconnection.

attributes.name: last_assessment_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent real-time or study-mode security assessment execution that evaluated this contingency scenario.

attributes.name: last_violation_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contingency most recently resulted in a thermal, voltage, or stability violation during security assessment. Null if no violations have been detected.

attributes.name: load_at_risk_mw
attributes.description: Total customer load in megawatts that could be interrupted or at risk of interruption if this contingency occurs and results in cascading outages or system instability.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this contingency record was most recently modified, supporting change tracking and audit requirements.

attributes.name: monitoring_elements_count
attributes.description: Count of transmission elements (lines, transformers, interfaces) that are monitored for thermal overload, voltage violation, or stability issues when this contingency is applied in security assessment.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Classification
attributes.description: NERC CIP impact rating classification for the elements involved in this contingency, indicating the cyber security and physical security requirements applicable to these assets.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-002 BES Cyber System Categorization

attributes.name: nerc_region
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Regional Entity
attributes.description: NERC regional entity with reliability oversight for this contingency scenario (e.g., WECC, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, Texas RE).

attributes.name: oms_zone_code
attributes.description: Identifier linking this contingency to the OMS zone for coordination of planned and unplanned outage management and customer impact assessment.

attributes.name: primary_element_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the primary transmission or generation element that is removed in this contingency scenario, as defined in the EMS network model.
attributes.references: NERC MOD-032 Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

attributes.name: primary_element_type
attributes.description: Type classification of the primary element that is removed or fails in this contingency scenario.

attributes.name: primary_element_voltage_kv
attributes.business_glossary_term: Primary Element Voltage Level in Kilovolts (kV)
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts of the primary element involved in the contingency scenario.

attributes.name: probability_class
attributes.description: Qualitative assessment of the likelihood of this contingency occurring based on historical outage data, equipment reliability, and operational experience.

attributes.name: probability_value
attributes.description: Quantitative probability estimate (0.0 to 1.0) representing the annual likelihood of this contingency scenario occurring, derived from historical reliability data and risk assessment models.
attributes.references: IEEE 762 Standard for Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

attributes.name: real_time_assessment_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in the real-time security assessment (RTSA) engine that runs continuously in the EMS to monitor system security.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: Code identifying the RTO or ISO that has operational or planning jurisdiction over this contingency scenario (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE).

attributes.name: secondary_element_name
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Null for single-element contingencies.

attributes.name: secondary_element_type
attributes.description: Type classification of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Set to 'none' for single-element (N-1) contingencies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transmission_line|transformer|generator|bus|shunt_device|hvdc_link|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: severity_rating
attributes.description: Assessment of the potential impact severity if this contingency were to occur, considering load at risk, voltage collapse potential, cascading outage risk, and system stability margin degradation.

attributes.name: stability_margin_percent
attributes.description: Percentage margin between the current operating point and the stability limit (voltage collapse point or transient stability limit) under this contingency scenario. Higher values indicate greater system security.

attributes.name: state_code
attributes.description: Two-letter state or province code where the primary contingency element is located, used for regulatory reporting and jurisdictional coordination.

attributes.name: study_mode_enabled
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in offline study-mode security assessments used for day-ahead planning, seasonal studies, and long-term transmission planning.

attributes.name: thermal_limit_mva
attributes.description: Maximum thermal capacity in MVA for the most critical monitored element under this contingency scenario, representing the binding constraint for system operations.

attributes.name: voltage_limit_lower_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Lower Voltage Limit in Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 0.90 to 0.95 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.

attributes.name: voltage_limit_upper_pu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Upper Voltage Limit in Per Unit (pu)
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 1.05 to 1.10 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.

products.name: security_assessment
products.description: Records results of real-time and study-mode security assessments (contingency analysis, power flow, voltage stability) performed by the EMS. Captures assessment timestamp, study type, number of violations found, worst-case contingency, thermal overload count, voltage violation count, and recommended corrective actions. Supports operator situational awareness and NERC reliability compliance.

attributes.name: security_assessment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the security assessment record. Primary key.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the balancing area under which this security assessment was conducted.

attributes.name: control_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the control zone where this security assessment was performed.

attributes.name: grid_contingency_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the contingency that resulted in the most severe violations or highest risk during this assessment.

attributes.name: assessment_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Total execution time of the security assessment in seconds, from initiation to completion.

attributes.name: assessment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the security assessment execution: completed (successfully finished), in-progress (currently running), failed (error during execution), aborted (manually stopped), or pending-review (awaiting operator validation).

attributes.name: assessment_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the security assessment was executed by the Energy Management System (EMS). This is the principal business event timestamp for the assessment.

attributes.name: assessment_type
attributes.description: The type of security assessment performed: real-time (operational), study-mode (what-if analysis), post-contingency (after event), pre-contingency (preventive), seasonal (long-term planning), or planning (future scenario).

attributes.name: contingency_count
attributes.description: Total number of contingencies (N-1, N-2, etc.) analyzed during this security assessment.

attributes.name: convergence_iterations
attributes.description: Number of iterations required for the power flow calculation to converge during the assessment.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether corrective actions are required to resolve violations identified in this assessment (True = corrective actions needed, False = no actions needed).

attributes.name: corrective_action_summary
attributes.description: Summary of recommended corrective actions to address violations, such as generation redispatch, load shedding, switching operations, or voltage control adjustments.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this security assessment record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: ems_system_code
attributes.description: Identifier of the Energy Management System (EMS) that performed this security assessment.

attributes.name: max_thermal_loading_pct
attributes.description: The highest thermal loading percentage observed on any transmission element during the assessment, expressed as a percentage of the element's rated capacity.

attributes.name: max_voltage_pu
attributes.description: The highest voltage level observed at any bus during the assessment, expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage.

attributes.name: min_voltage_pu
attributes.description: The lowest voltage level observed at any bus during the assessment, expressed in per-unit (pu) of nominal voltage.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this security assessment record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: nerc_compliance_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Compliance Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the assessment results meet NERC reliability compliance requirements (True = compliant, False = non-compliant).

attributes.name: notification_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the Reliability Coordinator or other stakeholders were notified of critical assessment results.

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the system operator regarding the assessment results, actions taken, or special conditions observed.

attributes.name: peak_demand_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the assessment was performed during a peak demand period (True = peak demand, False = off-peak).

attributes.name: power_flow_convergence_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the power flow calculation converged successfully during the assessment (True = converged, False = did not converge).

attributes.name: reliability_coordinator_notified
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the Reliability Coordinator was notified of critical violations found in this assessment (True = notified, False = not notified).

attributes.name: reserve_margin_mw
attributes.description: Available operating reserve margin in megawatts at the time of the assessment, representing the difference between available generation and current load.

attributes.name: scada_snapshot_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Snapshot ID
attributes.description: Identifier of the SCADA data snapshot used as the base case for this security assessment.

attributes.name: season
attributes.description: The season during which the security assessment was performed: winter, spring, summer, or fall. Seasonal conditions impact load patterns and generation availability.

attributes.name: stability_violation_count
attributes.description: Number of stability violations (transient, voltage, or oscillatory stability) detected during dynamic security assessment.

attributes.name: study_case_name
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the study case or scenario used for this assessment, typically defined in the EMS study environment.

attributes.name: thermal_overload_count
attributes.description: Number of thermal overload violations detected on transmission lines, transformers, or other equipment during the assessment.

attributes.name: total_generation_mw
attributes.description: Total system generation in megawatts at the time of the security assessment.

attributes.name: total_load_mw
attributes.description: Total system load in megawatts at the time of the security assessment.

attributes.name: violation_count
attributes.description: Total number of reliability violations (thermal, voltage, stability) detected across all contingencies in this assessment.

attributes.name: voltage_violation_count
attributes.description: Number of voltage limit violations (high or low voltage) detected at buses or substations during the assessment.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Weather condition at the time of the assessment that may impact system reliability: normal, extreme-heat, extreme-cold, high-wind, storm, ice, or fog. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: normal|extreme-heat|extreme-cold|high-wind|storm|ice|fog — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: worst_contingency_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the worst-case contingency scenario, including affected equipment and outage conditions.

attributes.name: worst_violation_severity
attributes.description: Severity classification of the most critical violation found during the assessment: critical (immediate action required), high (urgent attention), medium (monitor closely), low (minor concern), or none (no violations).

products.name: operator_log
products.description: Chronological log of operator actions, observations, and communications recorded in the grid operations control room. Each entry captures timestamp, operator ID, shift, log entry type (action, alarm acknowledgment, communication, note), associated asset or event, and free-text narrative. Serves as the official operational record for post-event analysis, regulatory audits, and NERC CIP compliance.

attributes.name: operator_log_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each operator log entry in the grid operations control room. Primary key for the operator_log data product.

attributes.name: alarm_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Alarm ID
attributes.description: The alarm identifier from the SCADA or EMS system that triggered or is associated with this log entry. Populated for alarm_acknowledgment entry types. Enables traceability from the operator log back to the originating SCADA alarm in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007-6, OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: asset_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.

attributes.name: control_zone_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grid control zone or balancing area associated with this log entry. Links to the gridops.control_zone master record for geographic and operational context.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed control room operator who authored this log entry. Links to the workforce/employee master record. Required for NERC CIP personnel accountability and shift responsibility tracking.

attributes.name: primary_operator_person_id
attributes.description: Reference to the licensed control room operator who authored this log entry. Links to the workforce/employee master record. Required for NERC CIP personnel accountability and shift responsibility tracking.

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.

attributes.name: reliability_event_id
attributes.description: Reference to a NERC reliability event or OMS outage event that this log entry is associated with. Null if the entry is not tied to a specific reliability event. Enables correlation of operator actions to event timelines.

attributes.name: safety_audit_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to safety.safety_audit. Business justification: Safety audits review operator logs to verify compliance with operating procedures and identify violations.

attributes.name: scada_alarm_alarm_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Alarm ID
attributes.description: The alarm identifier from the SCADA or EMS system that triggered or is associated with this log entry. Populated for alarm_acknowledgment entry types. Enables traceability from the operator log back to the originating SCADA alarm in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007-6, OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Point ID
attributes.description: The SCADA data point or tag identifier from OSIsoft PI Historian associated with the measurement or control action referenced in this log entry. Enables direct linkage to real-time operational data for post-event analysis.

attributes.name: shift_id
attributes.description: Reference to the operational shift during which this log entry was created. Enables shift-level aggregation of events, handover documentation, and accountability reporting.

attributes.name: shift_supervisor_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the shift supervisor who reviewed or approved this log entry. Required for entries of critical or high priority. Supports supervisory accountability and NERC CIP-004 personnel management compliance.

attributes.name: ace_mw
attributes.description: The Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) recorded at the time of the log entry. ACE is the real-time difference between actual and scheduled interchange, adjusted for frequency deviation. Critical metric for balancing area control and NERC BAL-001 compliance.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_c
attributes.description: Ambient air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the time of the log entry. Relevant for thermal loading analysis, equipment derating, and weather-related event context.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this log entry was formally approved as part of the official operational record. Null if not yet approved. Required for regulatory audit trail integrity.

attributes.name: asset_identifier
attributes.description: Human-readable asset identifier or tag number (e.g., substation name, feeder ID, equipment tag) as recorded by the operator at time of entry. Preserved as entered to maintain the original operational record even if the asset master record changes.
attributes.references: ISO 55000 Asset Management, Esri ArcGIS GIS Asset Registry

attributes.name: asset_type
attributes.description: Type classification of the grid asset referenced in this log entry. Supports asset-type-specific filtering and analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: substation|transformer|feeder|generator|transmission_line|bus|breaker|capacitor_bank|relay|meter — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: attachment_reference
attributes.description: File path, document management system reference, or URL pointing to supporting documentation attached to this log entry (e.g., switching order PDF, alarm printout, event report). Null if no attachment.

attributes.name: cip_classification
attributes.description: NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) impact classification of the asset or action referenced in this log entry. Determines the level of cybersecurity and physical security controls applicable. Required for NERC CIP-002 asset categorization compliance.

attributes.name: communication_method
attributes.description: The method or channel used for the communication recorded in this log entry. Relevant for NERC COM-001 compliance which mandates reliable communication facilities for grid operators.

attributes.name: communication_party
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the external or internal party involved in a communication log entry (e.g., RTO/ISO operator name, neighboring utility, field crew ID, supervisor name). Populated for communication entry types.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this log entry requires a follow-up corrective action, work order, or remediation activity. True = a corrective action has been identified and must be tracked. Supports NERC CIP corrective action plan (CAP) tracking.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this log record was first persisted in the data platform (Silver layer). Distinct from entry_timestamp (when the operator created the entry) and event_occurred_timestamp (when the event happened). Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: dr_dispatch_mw
attributes.description: The quantity of Demand Response (DR) capacity dispatched or curtailed in Megawatts (MW) as recorded in this log entry. Populated for demand_response entry category entries.

attributes.name: entry_category
attributes.description: Operational category classifying the functional area of the grid operation described in this log entry. Supports domain-specific filtering for post-event analysis and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|demand_response|frequency_regulation|voltage_control|outage|switching|environmental|safety|administrative — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: entry_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the log entry within the control room logging workflow. 'draft' = in progress; 'submitted' = finalized by operator; 'reviewed' = reviewed by shift supervisor; 'approved' = approved for official record; 'voided' = invalidated with reason.

attributes.name: entry_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (UTC) when the operator created or submitted the log entry in the Energy Management System (EMS) or control room logging system. This is the principal real-world event time for the log record. Conforms to yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.
attributes.references: NERC FAC-001, NERC CIP-007-6, FERC Order 693

attributes.name: entry_type
attributes.description: Categorical discriminator classifying the nature of the log entry. 'action' = operator-initiated grid action; 'alarm_acknowledgment' = SCADA/EMS alarm acknowledged; 'communication' = inter-operator or inter-entity communication; 'observation' = operational observation or reading; 'switching_order' = switching order execution step; 'note' = general operational note.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007-6, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS Log Standards

attributes.name: event_occurred_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (UTC) when the actual grid event, alarm, or operational action physically occurred, as distinct from when the operator recorded it. Critical for post-event timeline reconstruction and NERC reliability event analysis. May differ from entry_timestamp due to logging latency.

attributes.name: frequency_hz
attributes.description: The measured system frequency in Hertz (Hz) at the time of the log entry, as recorded by the operator or captured from SCADA. Relevant for frequency regulation events and under-frequency load shedding actions. Nominal value is 60.0000 Hz for North American grids.

attributes.name: generation_mw
attributes.description: The measured or dispatched generation output in Megawatts (MW) referenced in this log entry. Relevant for generation dispatch, curtailment, and unit commitment actions.

attributes.name: load_mw
attributes.description: The measured or observed load in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the log entry. Relevant for load shedding, demand response dispatch, and load balancing actions. Null if not applicable to the entry type.

attributes.name: log_entry_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable sequential identifier for the log entry (e.g., OL-2024-00123456). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory audits, NERC compliance filings, and post-event analysis reports.

attributes.name: narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative entered by the operator describing the action taken, observation made, alarm acknowledged, or communication recorded. This is the primary payload of the log entry and serves as the official operational record for post-event analysis, regulatory audits, and NERC CIP compliance reviews.
attributes.references: NERC EOP-004-3, NERC CIP-008-6, FERC Order 693

attributes.name: nerc_reportable
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this log entry is associated with a NERC-reportable reliability event per NERC EOP-004 disturbance reporting thresholds. True = event meets NERC reporting criteria and must be submitted to NERC/DOE via OE-417 or similar form.

attributes.name: nerc_standard_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: NERC (North American Electric Reliability Corporation) Standard Reference
attributes.description: The specific NERC Reliability Standard(s) applicable to the action or event described in this log entry (e.g., BAL-001, EOP-004, CIP-007). Supports compliance mapping and regulatory audit traceability.
attributes.references: NERC Reliability Standards Catalog, FERC Order 693

attributes.name: outage_ticket_number
attributes.description: The outage ticket or trouble order number from the OMS associated with this log entry. Populated when the log entry relates to an active outage event. Enables correlation between operator actions and outage management workflows.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS, NERC EOP-004-3

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operational priority or severity level assigned to the log entry, indicating urgency and potential grid impact. 'critical' entries typically correspond to NERC reportable events or imminent reliability threats.

attributes.name: puc_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this log entry is associated with an event that must be reported to the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Public Service Commission (PSC) per state regulatory requirements. True = state regulatory reporting obligation exists.
attributes.references: State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Reporting Requirements, PSC Regulations

attributes.name: reviewed_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the shift supervisor reviewed this log entry. Null if not yet reviewed. Part of the log entry lifecycle audit trail required for NERC compliance.

attributes.name: source_log_reference
attributes.description: The native log or record identifier from the originating source system (EMS, DMS, OMS, SCADA). Enables traceability back to the system of record for data lineage and reconciliation purposes in the Silver layer.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The originating operational system from which this log entry was generated or ingested. 'ems' = Energy Management System; 'dms' = Distribution Management System; 'oms' = Outage Management System; 'scada' = SCADA system; 'pi_historian' = OSIsoft PI Historian; 'manual' = manually entered by operator.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

attributes.name: switching_order_number
attributes.description: The switching order number from the DMS/OMS system associated with this log entry. Populated for switching_order entry types. Links the operator log to the formal switching order workflow in GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS.
attributes.references: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS, NERC EOP-005

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this log record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks amendments, supervisor reviews, and status transitions. Required for Silver layer change data capture and audit trail completeness.

attributes.name: void_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation for why this log entry was voided or invalidated. Populated only when entry_status = 'voided'. Maintains audit trail integrity by preserving the reason for invalidation rather than deleting the record.

attributes.name: voltage_kv
attributes.description: The measured or observed voltage in kilovolts (kV) at the referenced asset or bus at the time of the log entry. Relevant for voltage control actions, voltage deviation events, and reactive power dispatch entries.

attributes.name: weather_condition
attributes.description: Prevailing weather condition at the time of the log entry as observed or reported by the operator. Relevant for weather-related outage events, load forecasting context, and post-event causal analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: clear|cloudy|rain|thunderstorm|snow|ice|high_wind|fog|extreme_heat — promote to reference product]

attributes.name: work_order_number
attributes.description: The Maximo EAM work order number associated with corrective or maintenance actions triggered by this log entry. Populated when corrective_action_required = True. Enables traceability from operational events to maintenance work execution.

products.name: alarm_event
products.description: Records each SCADA/EMS alarm generated from monitored grid assets including thermal overloads, voltage violations, equipment failures, communication loss, and protection system operations. Captures alarm point, alarm type, priority level (per ISA-18.2 alarm management standard), trigger value, threshold, acknowledgment status, acknowledging operator, shelving status, and time to acknowledge/clear. Supports alarm rationalization, operator performance review, and NERC CIP-007 compliance.

attributes.name: alarm_event_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the alarm event record. Primary key.

attributes.name: asset_registry_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, line, generator, etc.) associated with this alarm. Links to the enterprise asset management system.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the NERC-registered balancing area where the alarm occurred. Links to the gridops.balancing_area product.

attributes.name: control_zone_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the control zone or dispatch area responsible for this alarm. Links to the gridops.control_zone product.

attributes.name: distribution_switching_order_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the switching order associated with this alarm if the alarm was triggered during planned switching operations. Links to gridops.switching_order.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: User ID or employee number of the operator who acknowledged the alarm. Used for performance tracking and audit trails.

attributes.name: gridops_outage_event_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the associated outage event if this alarm is related to a customer outage or system disturbance. Links to the OMS (Outage Management System).

attributes.name: registry_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the physical grid asset (transformer, breaker, line, generator, etc.) associated with this alarm. Links to the enterprise asset management system.

attributes.name: scada_point_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the SCADA point or tag that generated this alarm. Links to the monitored asset or measurement point in the SCADA system.

attributes.name: shelved_by_operator_employee_id
attributes.description: User ID of the operator who shelved the alarm. Required for audit and compliance.

attributes.name: transmission_substation_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the substation where the alarmed asset is located. Null for transmission line or distributed asset alarms.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the maintenance or repair work order created in response to this alarm. Links to the EAM (Enterprise Asset Management) system.

attributes.name: acknowledged_by_operator_name
attributes.description: Full name of the operator who acknowledged the alarm. Denormalized for reporting convenience.

attributes.name: acknowledged_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the alarm has been acknowledged by an operator. True if acknowledged, False if still unacknowledged.

attributes.name: acknowledged_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alarm was acknowledged by an operator. Null if not yet acknowledged.

attributes.name: alarm_category
attributes.description: Business classification of the alarm condition: thermal_overload (conductor or transformer heating), voltage_violation (over/under voltage), frequency_deviation (grid frequency out of range), equipment_failure (device malfunction), communication_loss (telemetry failure), or protection_system (relay or breaker operation).

attributes.name: alarm_count
attributes.description: Number of times this alarm condition has occurred for this asset within the current analysis window. Used for alarm flood detection and nuisance alarm identification.

attributes.name: alarm_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the alarm condition, including context, potential causes, and recommended operator actions. Used for training and alarm rationalization.

attributes.name: alarm_message
attributes.description: Full alarm message text as presented to the operator in the SCADA/EMS system. Includes asset name, condition description, and measured value.

attributes.name: alarm_state
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the alarm: active (unacknowledged and condition persists), acknowledged (operator has seen it), cleared (condition returned to normal), shelved (temporarily disabled), suppressed (filtered by alarm management logic), or stale (communication lost).

attributes.name: alarm_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the alarm condition was detected and the alarm was triggered in the SCADA/EMS system. This is the operational event time, distinct from record creation time.
attributes.references: IEEE 1686 Substation Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) Cyber Security

attributes.name: alarm_type
attributes.description: Classification of the alarm based on the nature of the monitored condition: analog (threshold violation on continuous measurement), digital (discrete state change), calculated (derived condition), communication (loss of signal), equipment_status (device health), or protection_operation (relay trip).

attributes.name: cip_classification
attributes.description: NERC CIP impact classification of the asset or system that generated this alarm: high (critical cyber assets), medium (medium impact BES cyber systems), low (low impact BES cyber systems), or not_applicable.

attributes.name: cleared_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alarm condition returned to normal and the alarm was cleared. Null if alarm is still active.

attributes.name: ems_alarm_code
attributes.description: Native alarm identifier from the EMS system. Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trails.
attributes.references: IEC 61970 Energy Management System Application Program Interface (EMS-API)

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the GIS feature (point, line, polygon) representing the alarmed asset in the enterprise GIS system. Enables spatial analysis and map visualization.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the alarmed asset location. Used for spatial analysis and mobile workforce dispatch.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate (decimal degrees) of the alarmed asset location. Used for spatial analysis and mobile workforce dispatch.

attributes.name: nerc_reportable_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reportable Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alarm represents a condition that must be reported to NERC under reliability standards (e.g., Bulk Electric System disturbance, CIP cyber security event). True if reportable, False otherwise.

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Operator response priority assigned to the alarm per ISA-18.2 alarm rationalization methodology. Critical alarms require immediate action; informational alarms are for awareness only.

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this alarm event record was first inserted into the data platform. Distinct from alarm_timestamp (operational event time). Used for data lineage and audit.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this alarm event record was last modified in the data platform. Updated when alarm state changes (acknowledged, cleared, shelved).

attributes.name: shelved_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the alarm has been temporarily shelved (suppressed) by an operator. True if shelved, False otherwise. Shelving is used during maintenance or known abnormal conditions.

attributes.name: shelved_reason
attributes.description: Operator-entered justification for shelving the alarm (e.g., 'Planned maintenance on Transformer T-101', 'Known communication issue during storm').

attributes.name: shelved_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alarm was shelved. Null if not shelved.

attributes.name: suppressed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the alarm was automatically suppressed by alarm management logic (e.g., flood suppression, consequential alarm filtering). True if suppressed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: suppression_rule
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the alarm management rule that suppressed this alarm (e.g., 'Substation Lockout Flood Suppression', 'Communication Loss Consequential Filter').

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The configured threshold or setpoint that was exceeded to trigger the alarm (e.g., high limit, low limit, deadband). Null for digital/status alarms.

attributes.name: time_to_acknowledge_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds between alarm_timestamp and acknowledged_timestamp. Key performance indicator for operator response time per ISA-18.2.

attributes.name: time_to_clear_seconds
attributes.description: Elapsed time in seconds between alarm_timestamp and cleared_timestamp. Measures total alarm duration and system restoration time.

attributes.name: trigger_value
attributes.description: The measured value that triggered the alarm condition (e.g., actual current in amps, voltage in kV, temperature in Celsius, frequency in Hz). Null for digital/status alarms.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Engineering unit for the trigger_value and threshold_value fields (e.g., 'A' for amps, 'kV' for kilovolts, 'MW' for megawatts, 'Hz' for hertz, 'C' for Celsius, 'psi' for pressure).

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the circuit or equipment where the alarm occurred (e.g., 345, 138, 69, 13.8, 4.16).

products.name: energy_balance
products.description: Hourly and sub-hourly energy balance records for the balancing area capturing total generation (MWh), total load (MWh), net interchange (MWh), losses, and ACE (Area Control Error). Derived from SCADA telemetry and used for NERC BAL compliance reporting, settlement with RTOs/ISOs, and operational accounting. Represents the authoritative near-real-time energy accounting record for the balancing area.
products.reference: NERC BAL / Balancing Area Energy Accounting

attributes.name: energy_balance_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each energy balance record in the balancing area. Primary key for the energy_balance data product.

attributes.name: aggregation_group_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to der.aggregation_group. Business justification: Energy balance reports are broken out by aggregation groups for market settlement and DER performance analysis.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Reference to the NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this energy balance record applies. Links to the balancing_area master record.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007, NERC BAL-001 operator accountability

attributes.name: gl_account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Energy Balance records are posted to the General Ledger for financial statements and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: person_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.
attributes.references: NERC CIP-007, NERC BAL-001 operator accountability

attributes.name: product_rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.rate_schedule. Business justification: Settlement report requires applying the correct rate schedule to each balancing area energy balance for billing compliance.

attributes.name: regulatory_rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Energy balance statements are submitted as part of rate‑case settlements; linking provides traceability to the specific rate case.

attributes.name: ace_average_mw
attributes.description: Average Area Control Error (ACE) over the interval period in Megawatts (MW). Used for NERC Control Performance Standard (CPS1/CPS2) compliance calculations and regulatory reporting to NERC and state PUCs.

attributes.name: ace_mw
attributes.description: Area Control Error (ACE) for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). ACE = (Actual Net Interchange – Scheduled Net Interchange) – 10B(Actual Frequency – Scheduled Frequency). Key NERC BAL-001 compliance metric measuring real-time generation-load balance.

attributes.name: actual_interchange_mwh
attributes.description: Actual metered energy interchange across balancing area tie-lines during the interval, expressed in MWh. Compared against scheduled_interchange_mwh to compute interchange deviation for NERC BAL compliance.

attributes.name: cps1_score
attributes.description: NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score for the interval, expressed as a percentage. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE relative to frequency deviation. NERC requires a minimum 100% CPS1 score on a rolling 12-month basis.

attributes.name: cps2_violation_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the balancing area exceeded the NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) ACE limit (L10) during this interval. True = CPS2 violation occurred; False = within limits. Triggers mandatory NERC reporting when True.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this energy balance record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse, typically upon ingestion from SCADA/PI Historian or EMS. Audit trail field for data lineage.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 data retention, FERC Order 890

attributes.name: data_quality_code
attributes.description: Quality indicator for the energy balance record derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry quality flags. 'good' = validated telemetry; 'suspect' = questionable reading requiring review; 'estimated' = gap-filled or interpolated; 'bad' = failed quality check; 'missing' = no telemetry received.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI quality codes, NERC BAL-001 data quality requirements

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the primary source system from which this energy balance record was derived. 'scada' = GE PowerOn SCADA telemetry; 'pi_historian' = OSIsoft PI Historian; 'ems' = Energy Management System calculated; 'manual' = operator-entered; 'estimated' = gap-filled estimate.

attributes.name: der_net_injection_mwh
attributes.description: Net energy injected into the grid from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, battery storage, and small-scale generation during the interval, expressed in MWh. Tracked via DERMS integration.
attributes.references: FERC Order 2222, NERC BAL-001, State NEM tariffs

attributes.name: dr_response_mwh
attributes.description: Energy reduction achieved through Demand Response (DR) dispatch during the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents load curtailment from DR programs activated by the EMS/DERMS. Used for DR settlement and NERC BAL compliance.
attributes.references: FERC Order 745, NERC BAL-002, FERC Order 2222

attributes.name: eia_930_reported_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this energy balance record has been included in an EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. True = reported to EIA; False = pending submission. Supports regulatory reporting completeness tracking.

attributes.name: eia_ba_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Energy Information Administration (EIA) Balancing Authority Code
attributes.description: EIA-assigned balancing authority code for the reporting entity. Required for EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. Uniquely identifies the balancing authority in EIA's national energy data system.

attributes.name: finalized_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this energy balance record was promoted from 'preliminary' to 'final' status following validation. Marks the completion of the operational accounting close for the interval.

attributes.name: fossil_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy generated from fossil fuel sources (natural gas, coal, oil) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Used for emissions reporting to EPA and EIA.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923, EPA Clean Air Act reporting, FERC Form 1

attributes.name: frequency_bias_mw_per_hz
attributes.description: The frequency bias setting (B) applied in the ACE calculation formula for this interval, expressed in MW/Hz. Represents the balancing area's contribution to primary frequency response. Filed annually with NERC.

attributes.name: frequency_hz
attributes.description: Average system frequency measured in Hertz (Hz) during the interval. Nominal value is 60.000 Hz for the North American interconnection. Deviations from nominal drive ACE calculations and frequency regulation dispatch.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-003, NERC BAL-004, NERC FAC-001

attributes.name: inadvertent_interchange_mwh
attributes.description: Accumulated inadvertent energy interchange for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the difference between actual and scheduled interchange that must be repaid to neighboring balancing areas per NERC BAL-005 payback requirements.

attributes.name: interconnection
attributes.description: North American electrical interconnection to which this balancing area belongs. Determines synchronous frequency reference and reliability coordinator jurisdiction.

attributes.name: interval_duration_minutes
attributes.description: Duration of the energy balance interval in minutes (e.g., 5, 15, 30, 60). Distinguishes sub-hourly from hourly records and supports aggregation logic.

attributes.name: interval_end_timestamp
attributes.description: The ending timestamp of the energy accounting interval. Together with interval_start_timestamp defines the precise measurement window for this balance record.

attributes.name: interval_start_timestamp
attributes.description: The beginning timestamp of the energy accounting interval (hourly or sub-hourly) for which this balance record is computed. Derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry. Conforms to ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, EIA Form 930

attributes.name: load_forecast_error_mwh
attributes.description: Difference between actual total load and forecasted load for the interval, expressed in MWh (actual minus forecast). Positive value indicates load exceeded forecast; negative indicates load was below forecast. Used to evaluate forecasting accuracy and improve EMS models.

attributes.name: load_forecast_mwh
attributes.description: Forecasted energy load for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Generated by the EMS load forecasting module prior to the operating interval. Used to compute forecast error and support dispatch planning.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, EIA Form 930

attributes.name: nerc_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this energy balance interval is fully compliant with applicable NERC BAL reliability standards (BAL-001, BAL-002, BAL-003, BAL-005). True = compliant; False = one or more NERC BAL standard violations detected. Triggers compliance workflow when False.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-002, NERC BAL-003, NERC BAL-005

attributes.name: nerc_tag_number
attributes.description: NERC e-Tag identifier associated with the scheduled interchange transactions contributing to this energy balance interval. Used for cross-referencing with NERC e-Tag system for interchange scheduling and curtailment tracking.

attributes.name: net_interchange_mwh
attributes.description: Net energy exchanged across the balancing area boundary during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Positive value indicates net export; negative value indicates net import. Computed as sum of all scheduled and actual tie-line flows.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-005, FERC Order 890

attributes.name: nuclear_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy generated from nuclear sources within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Reported separately per NRC and EIA requirements.

attributes.name: operating_date
attributes.description: The calendar date (in local prevailing time) to which this energy balance interval belongs. Used for daily aggregation, settlement, and regulatory reporting aligned to the operating day.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 930, FERC Order 890

attributes.name: operating_hour
attributes.description: The hour of the operating day (0–23) in which this interval falls, expressed in local prevailing time. Used for hourly aggregation, TOU analysis, and RTO/ISO settlement hour alignment.

attributes.name: operating_reserve_mw
attributes.description: Total operating reserve available in the balancing area at the start of the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-002, NERC BAL-003, RTO/ISO reserve requirements

attributes.name: record_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of the energy balance record indicating its processing and settlement state. 'preliminary' = near-real-time estimate; 'final' = validated operational accounting; 'revised' = corrected after initial finalization; 'settled' = accepted by RTO/ISO for financial settlement; 'void' = invalidated record.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, RTO/ISO settlement protocols

attributes.name: renewable_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy generated from renewable sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, biomass) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Supports Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking and IRP reporting.
attributes.references: EIA Form 923, FERC Form 1, State RPS requirements

attributes.name: revision_number
attributes.description: Sequential revision counter for this energy balance record. Starts at 0 for the initial preliminary record and increments with each correction or resettlement. Supports audit trail and version management for regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890 data retention requirements

attributes.name: revision_reason
attributes.description: Free-text description of the reason for the most recent revision to this energy balance record (e.g., 'meter data correction', 'SCADA telemetry gap fill', 'RTO settlement adjustment'). Populated only when revision_number > 0.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Code
attributes.description: Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) with which this balancing area is affiliated for market settlement and reliability coordination (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE).
attributes.references: FERC Order 888, FERC Order 2000, NERC registration

attributes.name: scheduled_interchange_mwh
attributes.description: Total energy interchange scheduled across balancing area tie-lines for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or intra-day scheduled position prior to real-time deviations.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-005, FERC Order 890

attributes.name: settled_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this energy balance record was accepted and confirmed by the RTO/ISO for financial settlement. Marks the completion of the market settlement lifecycle for the interval.

attributes.name: settlement_period_type
attributes.description: Identifies the market settlement period type for this energy balance record. 'real_time' = RTM interval data; 'day_ahead' = DAM scheduled position; 'final_settlement' = post-operating-day settlement; 'resettlement' = corrected settlement after dispute resolution.
attributes.references: FERC Order 890, RTO/ISO tariff settlement protocols

attributes.name: spinning_reserve_mw
attributes.description: Spinning (synchronized) reserve available in the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MW. Subset of operating_reserve_mw representing generation online and capable of immediate response. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.

attributes.name: total_generation_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy generated within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Aggregates all generation resources including fossil fuel, nuclear, and renewable sources. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 923, FERC Form 1

attributes.name: total_load_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy consumed by load within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Represents native load plus losses. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 930, FERC Order 890

attributes.name: transmission_losses_mwh
attributes.description: Estimated electrical energy lost in transmission and distribution within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Used in energy accounting identity: Generation = Load + Net Interchange + Losses.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001, FERC Form 1, EIA Form 930

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this energy balance record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Updated on each revision, status change, or data quality correction.
attributes.references: NERC BAL-001 data retention, FERC Order 890

products.name: transmission_limit
products.description: Master records for thermal, voltage, and stability limits on transmission facilities (lines, transformers, flowgates, interfaces) enforced in real-time operations. Captures normal rating (MVA/MW), emergency rating (15-min/4-hr), load dump rating, seasonal and ambient-adjusted ratings, applicable contingency, limit source (thermal/voltage/stability), and effective date. These limits are the hard constraints enforced by EMS security analysis and operator dispatch decisions per NERC FAC-008.
products.reference: EMS Facility Rating / Transmission Operating Limit (TOL)

attributes.name: transmission_limit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the transmission limit record. Primary key for this entity.

attributes.name: balancing_area_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Transmission limits are defined per balancing area; FK adds relational context.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the transmission engineer or reliability coordinator who approved this limit for operational use.

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the transmission facility (line, transformer, flowgate, interface) to which this limit applies.

attributes.name: ambient_temperature_c
attributes.description: Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at which the limit rating was calculated. Used for dynamic rating adjustments.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which this transmission limit was formally approved for enforcement in real-time operations.

attributes.name: contingency_name
attributes.description: Name of the contingency scenario (e.g., N-1, N-2 outage) under which this limit applies. Identifies the specific outage condition that triggers this constraint.

attributes.name: contingency_type
attributes.description: Classification of the contingency: N-1 (single element outage), N-2 (double contingency), base case (no outage), or extreme event.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission limit record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: dynamic_rating_enabled
attributes.description: Indicates whether dynamic line rating (real-time adjustment based on weather and conductor temperature) is enabled for this facility. True if enabled, False otherwise.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date from which this transmission limit becomes active and enforceable in real-time operations and EMS security analysis.

attributes.name: emergency_rating_15min_mva
attributes.description: Short-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 15 minutes without damage, used during contingency conditions.

attributes.name: emergency_rating_4hr_mva
attributes.description: Long-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 4 hours, typically used for post-contingency load relief operations.

attributes.name: ems_limit_code
attributes.description: Identifier of this limit record in the Energy Management System (EMS) used for real-time security analysis and dispatch.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date on which this transmission limit expires or is superseded by a new limit. Null if the limit is open-ended.

attributes.name: ferc_jurisdiction
attributes.business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Jurisdiction Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission facility and its limits fall under FERC jurisdiction (interstate transmission). True if FERC-jurisdictional, False otherwise.

attributes.name: gis_feature_reference
attributes.description: Identifier of the corresponding transmission facility feature in the GIS system, used for geospatial analysis and mapping.

attributes.name: limit_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes providing additional context, operational instructions, or special conditions related to this transmission limit.

attributes.name: limit_source
attributes.description: Origin of the limit value: thermal analysis, voltage analysis, stability study, manufacturer equipment rating, field test measurement, or engineering judgment.

attributes.name: limit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the limit record: active (enforced in EMS), inactive, suspended (temporarily not enforced), pending approval, or retired.

attributes.name: limit_type
attributes.description: Physical constraint type: thermal (conductor heating), voltage (bus voltage deviation), stability (transient/voltage/oscillatory stability limits).

attributes.name: load_dump_rating_mva
attributes.description: Maximum load that can be shed or transferred through this facility during emergency load dump or load shedding operations.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this transmission limit record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: nerc_cip_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Classification
attributes.description: NERC CIP impact classification of the facility: high, medium, low, or not applicable. Determines cybersecurity and physical security requirements.

attributes.name: normal_rating_mva
attributes.description: Continuous normal operating limit in megavolt-amperes (MVA) under normal ambient and system conditions. This is the baseline thermal or transfer capability limit.

attributes.name: normal_rating_mw
attributes.description: Continuous normal operating limit in megawatts (MW) for real power transfer. Used for flowgates and interfaces where MW is the primary constraint metric.

attributes.name: rto_iso_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
attributes.description: Code of the RTO or ISO that has operational authority over this transmission facility and enforces these limits in market operations.

attributes.name: scada_monitored
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transmission limit is actively monitored in real-time via SCADA telemetry. True if monitored, False otherwise.

attributes.name: season_code
attributes.description: Season during which this limit applies: summer, winter, spring, fall, or year-round. Seasonal limits reflect ambient temperature and load pattern variations.

attributes.name: seasonal_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to base ratings to account for seasonal ambient temperature variations (e.g., summer de-rating, winter up-rating). Typically ranges from 0.8 to 1.2.

attributes.name: study_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier or document name of the engineering study (thermal, voltage, or stability study) that established this limit.

attributes.name: voltage_level_kv
attributes.description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the transmission facility (e.g., 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV).

attributes.name: voltage_limit_high_kv
attributes.description: Upper voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Exceeding this limit may cause equipment damage or system instability.

attributes.name: voltage_limit_low_kv
attributes.description: Lower voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Falling below this limit may cause voltage collapse or equipment malfunction.

products.name: weather_forecast
products.description: Weather forecast data integrated into grid operations for load forecasting, storm preparation, and renewable generation prediction including temperature, wind speed, cloud cover, and precipitation

attributes.name: weather_forecast_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for each weather forecast record.

attributes.name: cloud_cover_pct
attributes.description: Forecasted fraction of sky covered by clouds, expressed as a percentage.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Overall data quality assessment for the forecast record.

attributes.name: dew_point_c
attributes.description: Forecasted dew point temperature in degrees Celsius.

attributes.name: forecast_confidence_score
attributes.description: Numerical confidence rating (0‑100) assigned by the model to the forecast.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_hours
attributes.description: Number of hours ahead that the forecast covers.

attributes.name: forecast_horizon_type
attributes.description: Granularity of the forecast period (e.g., hourly, daily).

attributes.name: forecast_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time for which the forecast values are applicable.

attributes.name: humidity_adjustment_factor
attributes.description: Numeric factor used to modify forecast values for humidity influences.

attributes.name: humidity_pct
attributes.description: Forecasted relative humidity as a percentage.

attributes.name: is_adjusted_for_humidity
attributes.description: Indicates whether humidity‑based corrections were applied (true/false).

attributes.name: is_adjusted_for_terrain
attributes.description: Indicates whether terrain effects were applied to the forecast (true/false).

attributes.name: is_adjusted_for_time_of_day
attributes.description: Indicates whether diurnal effects were applied to the forecast (true/false).

attributes.name: issue_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the forecast was generated by the forecasting system.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude of the forecast location in decimal degrees.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude of the forecast location in decimal degrees.

attributes.name: model_version
attributes.description: Identifier of the forecasting model version used to generate the forecast.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free‑form comments or annotations from forecasters.

attributes.name: precipitation_inches
attributes.description: Forecasted total precipitation depth in inches.

attributes.name: pressure_hpa
attributes.description: Forecasted sea‑level atmospheric pressure in hectopascals.

attributes.name: probability_of_precipitation_pct
attributes.description: Forecasted likelihood of precipitation expressed as a percentage.

attributes.name: record_created_date
attributes.description: Calendar date when the forecast record was first stored in the lakehouse.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time of the most recent update to the forecast record.

attributes.name: severe_weather_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the forecast includes any severe weather conditions (true/false).

products.name: dispatch_participation
products.description: This association product represents the participation of meters in demand‑response dispatch events. Each record links one dr_dispatch_event to one meter and captures attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship.. Existence Justification: A demand‑response dispatch event can involve many meters, and a given meter can be dispatched in many events over time. The utility records each participation with status, actual reduction, and response timestamp, which are attributes of the participation itself. This relationship is actively managed by grid operations and is a distinct business entity.

attributes.name: dispatch_participation_id
attributes.description: Primary key for the dispatch_participation association

attributes.name: dr_dispatch_event_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Dispatch Participation - Dr Dispatch Event Id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to dr_dispatch_event

attributes.name: meter_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to meter

attributes.name: actual_reduction_mw
attributes.description: Actual MW reduction achieved by the meter during the dispatch event

attributes.name: participation_status
attributes.description: Status of the meter's participation in the dispatch event (e.g., responded, no‑response)

attributes.name: response_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the meter reported its response to the dispatch event

products.name: switching_order_material_allocation
products.description: Association table that records which material items are allocated to each grid operations switching order, including the quantity, unit of measure, and line status for each material requirement.. Existence Justification: A switching order often requires several spare parts or equipment items, and each material can be used in many different switching orders. The utility tracks the quantity, unit of measure, and status of each material assigned to a specific order, creating a distinct record for every order‑material pair.

attributes.name: switching_order_material_allocation_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Allocation - Switching Order Material Id
attributes.description: Primary key for the switching_order_material_allocation association

attributes.name: gridops_switching_order_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the switching order

attributes.name: material_master_id

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the material master

attributes.name: line_status

attributes.name: quantity
attributes.description: Amount of the material allocated to the switching order

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the allocated quantity (e.g., EA, KG)
